sentences.zh: 劉蒨，字惟馨，涪州人。

translations.literal: Liu Qian, styled Weixin, was a native of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qian, courtesy name Weixin, came from Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年進士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twelfth year of the Hongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 授戶科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor of the Household Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a supervising secretary in the Household Section.

sentences.zh: 劾戶部尚書掞鐘縱子受賕，論外戚慶雲侯、壽寧侯家人侵牟商利，阻壞鹺法，又論文選郎張彩顛倒銓政。

translations.literal: He impeached Minister of Revenue Si Zhong for indulging his son in accepting bribes; he argued that relatives of the marquises of Qingyun and Shouning encroached on commerce for profit and obstructed the salt monopoly, and he also charged Selection Bureau director Zhang Cai with perverting appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached the Minister of Revenue, Si Zhong, for allowing his son to take bribes; denounced the households of the Qingyun and Shouning marquises for profiteering at merchants' expense and undermining the salt laws; and accused Zhang Cai, director of the Selection Bureau, of reversing proper personnel policy.

sentences.zh: 有直聲。

translations.literal: He gained a reputation for forthrightness.
translations.idiomatic: He won a reputation for blunt integrity.

sentences.zh: 武宗踐阼，未數月，漸改孝宗之政。

translations.literal: When the Wuzong Emperor ascended the throne, within a few months he gradually altered the policies of the Xiaozong reign.
translations.idiomatic: Not many months after the Wuzong Emperor took the throne, government began to drift from the Xiaozong pattern.

sentences.zh: 蒨疏諫曰：「先帝大漸，召閣臣劉健、李東陽、謝遷於榻前，托以陛下。

translations.literal: Qian memorialized in remonstrance, saying: "When the late emperor was gravely ill, he summoned Grand Secretaries Liu Jian, Li Dongyang, and Xie Qian to his couch and entrusted Your Majesty to them.
translations.idiomatic: Qian submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "When the late emperor was near death, he called Grand Secretaries Liu Jian, Li Dongyang, and Xie Qian to his bedside and entrusted Your Majesty to them.

sentences.zh: 今梓宮未葬，德音猶存，而政事多乖，號令不信。

translations.literal: Now the imperial coffin is not yet buried and gracious edicts still stand, yet government affairs diverge widely and orders are not believed.
translations.idiomatic: The coffin has not yet been interred and his benevolent commands still stand, yet policy runs contrary to them and imperial words are no longer trusted.

sentences.zh: 張瑜、劉文泰方藥弗慎，致先帝升遐，不即加誅，容其奏辨。

translations.literal: Zhang Yu and Liu Wentai were careless with medicine and caused the late emperor's death, yet they were not immediately executed and were allowed to plead their case.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu and Liu Wentai mishandled the late emperor's medication and brought about his death, yet they were not promptly punished and were even permitted to defend themselves.

sentences.zh: 中官劉郎貽害河南，宜按治，僅調之薊州。

translations.literal: The eunuch Liu Lang brought harm to Henan and should have been investigated, yet he was merely transferred to Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Liu Lang had done harm in Henan and ought to have been prosecuted, but was only reassigned to Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 戶部奏汰冗員，兵部奏革傳奉，疏皆報罷。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue memorialized to cut redundant staff and the Ministry of War to abolish honorary appointments, yet both memorials were rejected.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue proposed eliminating superfluous personnel and the Ministry of War proposed abolishing honorary commissions, yet both memorials were set aside.

sentences.zh: 夫先帝留健等輔陛下，乃近日批答章奏，以恩侵法，以私掩公，是閣臣不得與聞，而左右近習陰有干預矣。

translations.literal: The late emperor left Jian and the others to assist Your Majesty, yet recently rescripts on memorials have used favor to encroach on law and private interest to cover public duty, so that the Grand Secretariat is kept uninformed while those close at hand secretly intervene.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor left Jian and his colleagues to assist Your Majesty, yet lately rescripts on memorials have let private favor override law and private interest mask public duty—the Grand Secretariat is kept out of the loop while intimates around the throne intervene in secret.

sentences.zh: 願遵遺命，信老成，政無大小，悉咨內閣，庶事無壅蔽，權不假竊。」

translations.literal: I pray that Your Majesty follow the dying command, trust seasoned ministers, and consult the Grand Secretariat on affairs great and small, so that nothing is blocked and power is not usurped.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to honor the deathbed charge, rely on experienced ministers, and refer every matter, large or small, to the Grand Secretariat, so that business is not obstructed and authority is not seized by others.

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: The memorial was noted.
translations.idiomatic: The court acknowledged receipt of the memorial.

sentences.zh: 正德元年，吏部尚書馬文升致仕，廷議推補。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde, Minister of Personnel Ma Wensheng retired, and the court debated whom to recommend to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengde, Ma Wensheng, Minister of Personnel, retired, and the court debated successors.

sentences.zh: 御史王時中以閔珪、劉大夏不宜在推舉之列。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Shizhong argued that Min Gui and Liu Daxia should not be on the recommended list.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Shizhong objected that Min Gui and Liu Daxia should not be among the nominees.

sentences.zh: 蒨恐耆德益疏，上疏極論其謬。

translations.literal: Fearing that worthy elders would be pushed further aside, Qian memorialized forcefully that this was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Qian, fearing that senior statesmen would be further marginalized, submitted a strong memorial refuting the proposal.

sentences.zh: 章下所司，是蒨言，詔為飭言官毋挾私妄奏。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the relevant offices; they upheld Qian's view, and an edict rebuked censors for lodging private accusations.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the responsible agencies, which sided with Qian; an edict then admonished censors not to lodge partisan charges.

sentences.zh: 孝宗在位時，深悉內臣出鎮之害，所遣皆慎選。

translations.literal: During the Xiaozong reign the court deeply understood the harm of sending eunuchs to command garrisons and chose appointees with care.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiaozong the court well understood the harm of eunuch military commanders and chose them cautiously.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾竊柄，盡召還之，而代以其黨。

translations.literal: When Liu Jin seized power he recalled them all and replaced them with his own followers.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liu Jin seized power he recalled them all and installed his own men.

sentences.zh: 蒨言：「用新人不若用舊人，猶養饑虎不若養飽虎。」

translations.literal: Qian said: "Employing new men is not as good as employing the old; it is like feeding a hungry tiger rather than a full one.
translations.idiomatic: Qian argued: "Using newcomers is worse than keeping the old—it is like feeding a hungry tiger instead of a sated one.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The court did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: His advice was ignored.

sentences.zh: 尋與給事中張文等極言時政缺失五事，忤旨，奪俸三月。

translations.literal: Soon, together with supervising secretary Zhang Wen and others, he spoke forcefully on five failures of current policy, offended the throne, and had his salary suspended for three months.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he and supervising secretary Zhang Wen and others sharply criticized five major policy failures, provoked imperial wrath, and were fined three months' salary.

sentences.zh: 劉健、謝遷去位，蒨與刑科給事中呂翀各抗章乞留，語侵瑾。

translations.literal: When Liu Jian and Xie Qian left office, Qian and Lu Chong of the Punishments Section each submitted a defiant memorial begging that they be retained, language that implicated Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jian and Xie Qian resigned, Qian and Lu Chong, supervising secretary of the Punishments Section, each submitted urgent memorials asking that they stay—language that implicated Jin.

sentences.zh: 先是，兵科都給事中艾洪劾中官高鳳侄得林營掌錦衣衛。

translations.literal: Earlier, chief supervising secretary of the Military Section Ai Hong had impeached the eunuch Gao Feng's nephew Delin for taking charge of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Ai Hong, chief supervising secretary of the Military Section, had impeached the eunuch Gao Feng's nephew Delin for taking command of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 諸疏傳至南京守備武靖伯趙承慶所，應天尹陸珩錄以示諸僚，兵部尚書林瀚聞而太息。

translations.literal: The memorials reached Nanjing at the garrison of Military Pacification Commissioner Zhao Chengqing; Prefect Lu Heng of Yingtian copied them for his colleagues, and Minister of War Lin Han sighed deeply on hearing of it.
translations.idiomatic: The memorials reached Nanjing at the post of Pacification Commissioner Zhao Chengqing; Yingtian prefect Lu Heng copied them for his colleagues, and War Minister Lin Han sighed heavily when he heard.

sentences.zh: 於是給事中戴銑、御史薄彥徽等，各馳疏極諫，請留健、遷。

translations.literal: Thereupon supervising secretaries Dai Xian, censor Bo Yanhui, and others each rushed memorials in strong remonstrance, asking that Jian and Qian be kept.
translations.idiomatic: Then supervising secretaries Dai Xian, censor Bo Yanhui, and others each sent urgent memorials in fierce remonstrance, begging that Jian and Qian be retained.

sentences.zh: 瑾等大怒，矯旨逮銑、彥徽等，下詔獄鞫治，並蒨、翀、洪俱廷杖削籍，承慶停半祿閑住，瀚、珩貶秩致仕。

translations.literal: Jin and his faction were furious; they forged an edict to arrest Xian, Yanhui, and the rest, tried them in the imperial prison, and had Qian, Chong, and Hong all beaten at court and struck from the rolls; Chengqing's stipend was halved and he was retired, while Han and Heng were demoted and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and his clique were enraged; they forged an edict to seize Xian, Yanhui, and the rest, tried them in the imperial prison, and had Qian, Chong, and Hong beaten at court and expelled from office; Chengqing's salary was halved and he was retired, while Han and Heng were demoted and sent home.

sentences.zh: 既而列健、遷等五十三人為奸黨，及翀、洪並預焉。

translations.literal: Later they listed Jian, Qian, and fifty-three others as a faction of traitors, and Chong and Hong were included.
translations.idiomatic: Later they branded Jian, Qian, and fifty-three others a treacherous faction, and Chong and Hong were named among them.

sentences.zh: 瑾敗，起蒨金華知府，舉治行卓異，未及遷輒告歸。

translations.literal: When Jin fell, Qian was reappointed prefect of Jinhua; his administration was outstanding, but before promotion he asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's fall Qian was appointed prefect of Jinhua; his governance was excellent, but he resigned before he could be promoted.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，起知長沙，遷江西副使卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing he was called to govern Changsha, then promoted to vice commissioner in Jiangxi, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiajing he was summoned to Changsha, then promoted to vice commissioner in Jiangxi, where he died in office.

sentences.zh: 御史範永奎訟於朝，特予祭葬。

translations.literal: Censor Fan Yongkui petitioned at court, and special sacrificial rites and burial honors were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Fan Yongkui appealed at court, and special sacrificial honors and burial were granted.

sentences.zh: 呂翀，廣信永豐人。

translations.literal: Lu Chong was a native of Yongfeng in Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chong came from Yongfeng in Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年進士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twelfth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 其請留健、遷言：「二臣不可聽去者有五。

translations.literal: In his plea to retain Jian and Qian he said: "There are five reasons the two ministers must not be allowed to go.
translations.idiomatic: In his plea to keep Jian and Qian he wrote: "There are five reasons these two ministers must not be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 孔子稱孟莊子之孝，以不改父之臣為難。

translations.literal: Confucius praised Meng Zhuangzi's filial piety for the difficulty of not changing his father's ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius praised Meng Zhuangzi's filial piety because he did not dismiss his father's ministers.

sentences.zh: 二臣皆先帝所簡以遺陛下，今陵土未幹，無故罷遣，何以慰在天之靈？

translations.literal: Both ministers were chosen by the late emperor and left to Your Majesty; the imperial tomb is not yet dry, yet they are dismissed without cause—how can this comfort his spirit in Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Both were handpicked by the late emperor for Your Majesty; the tomb earth is not yet dry, yet they are removed without cause—how can this console his spirit?

sentences.zh: 不可一也。

translations.literal: This cannot be allowed—first.
translations.idiomatic: The first reason they must stay.

sentences.zh: 二臣雖以老疾辭，實由言違計沮，不得其職而去。

translations.literal: Though the two ministers resigned citing age and illness, in truth policy was thwarted and their counsel blocked, and they left because they could not perform their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Though both cited age and illness, in truth their counsel was blocked and they left because they could not do their jobs.

sentences.zh: 陛下聽之，亦以其不善將順，非實有意優老也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty accepted their resignations because they would not simply agree with you, not because you truly wished to honor their age.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty let them go because they would not simply comply—not because you truly meant to honor their years.

sentences.zh: 在二臣得去就之義，在陛下有棄老成之嫌。

translations.literal: For the two ministers this was the propriety of leaving office; for Your Majesty it bears the stain of abandoning seasoned men.
translations.idiomatic: For them this was proper withdrawal; for Your Majesty it looks like casting aside experience.

sentences.zh: 不可二也。

translations.literal: This cannot be allowed—second.
translations.idiomatic: The second reason.

sentences.zh: 今民窮財殫，府藏虛罄，水旱盜賊、星象草木之變叠見雜出，萬一禍生不測，國無老成，誰與共事？

translations.literal: Now the people are impoverished, the treasury empty, floods, droughts, bandits, and strange signs in the heavens and on earth appear one after another; if unforeseen disaster should arise and the state lacks seasoned leaders, with whom will affairs be managed?
translations.idiomatic: The people are exhausted, the treasury bare, and floods, droughts, bandits, and omens in sky and earth come in waves; if calamity strikes and there are no elders in government, who will manage affairs?

sentences.zh: 不可三也。

translations.literal: This cannot be allowed—third.
translations.idiomatic: The third reason.

sentences.zh: 自古剛正者難容，柔順者易合。

translations.literal: Since antiquity the upright are hard to tolerate and the compliant are easy to join.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity the upright are hard to keep and the compliant easy to gather.

sentences.zh: 二臣既去，則柔順之人必進，將一聽陛下所為，非國家之福。

translations.literal: Once the two ministers are gone, compliant men will surely advance and Your Majesty will be left to do as you please—not a blessing to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Once they are gone, compliant men will advance and Your Majesty will do as you please—that is no blessing to the state.

sentences.zh: 不可四也。

translations.literal: This cannot be allowed—fourth.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth reason.

sentences.zh: 書曰『無遺壽耇』。

translations.literal: The Book says, "Do not cast aside the aged and venerable."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, "Do not abandon the elderly and venerable."

sentences.zh: 健等諳練有素，非新進可侔，今同日去國，天下後世將謂陛下喜新進而厭舊人。

translations.literal: Jian and the others are experienced and cannot be matched by newcomers; if they leave on the same day, all under Heaven will say Your Majesty favors the new and despises the old.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and his colleagues are seasoned and no newcomer can match them; if they leave together, the world will say Your Majesty loves the new and scorns the old.

sentences.zh: 不可五也。」

translations.literal: This cannot be allowed—fifth.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth reason.

sentences.zh: 既削籍歸，後起雲南僉事。

translations.literal: After he was struck from the rolls and returned home, he was later appointed assistant administration commissioner in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of rank and sent home, he was later appointed assistant administration commissioner in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 遷四川副使，修成都江堰以資灌溉，水利大興。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner in Sichuan, repaired the Dujiangyan works to aid irrigation, and water conservancy flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice commissioner in Sichuan, he restored the Dujiangyan irrigation works and greatly improved water management.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初卒。

translations.literal: He died early in the Jiajing reign.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 艾洪，濱州人。

translations.literal: Ai Hong was a native of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ai Hong came from Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the ninth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 授兵科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary of the Military Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was made supervising secretary of the Military Section.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，詔清核騰驤諸衛及在京七十二衛軍。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne, an edict ordered a thorough audit of the Tengxiang guards and the seventy-two capital garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong ascended, an edict ordered a full audit of the Tengxiang guards and the seventy-two capital garrisons.

sentences.zh: 給事中葛嵩剔抉無所徇，得各監局占役者七千五百余人，有旨送各營備操。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Ge Song investigated without favor and found more than seventy-five hundred men illegally held for service by the various directorates and offices; an edict ordered them sent to camps for drill.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Song, supervising secretary, investigated impartially and found more than 7,500 men illegally held for service by the directorates; an edict ordered them sent to camps for training.

sentences.zh: 既而中官魏興、蕭壽等撓之，格不行。

translations.literal: Later eunuchs Wei Xing, Xiao Shou, and others obstructed it, and the order was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs Wei Xing and Xiao Shou then blocked enforcement and the order lapsed.

sentences.zh: 洪率同官抗論，竟不能得。

translations.literal: Hong led his colleagues in protest but ultimately could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Hong led his colleagues in protest but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 又劾英國公張懋、懷寧侯孫應爵、新寧伯譚佑、彭城伯張信，並請斥陜西鎮監劉雲、薊州鎮監劉瑯阝。

translations.literal: He also impeached the Duke of Ying Zhang Mao, Marquis of Huaining Sun Yingjue, Baron of Xinning Tan You, and Baron of Pengcheng Zhang Xin, and asked that the garrison eunuchs Liu Yun of Shaanxi and Liu Lang of Jizhou be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Zhang Mao, Duke of Ying, Sun Yingjue, Marquis of Huaining, Tan You, Baron of Xinning, and Zhang Xin, Baron of Pengcheng, and asked that garrison eunuchs Liu Yun of Shaanxi and Liu Lang of Jizhou be removed.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The court did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The throne did not act.

sentences.zh: 雲尋調南京守備，乞以其養子偉為錦衣千戶。

translations.literal: Yun was soon transferred to Nanjing as commandant; he asked that his adopted son Wei be made a thousand-household of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was soon transferred to Nanjing as commandant and asked that his adopted son Wei be made a thousand-household of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 洪復率同官劾之，事乃寢。

translations.literal: Hong again led his colleagues in impeachment, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Hong again led his colleagues in impeachment, and the request was dropped.

sentences.zh: 洪在兵科久，諫疏多可稱。

translations.literal: Hong served long in the Military Section and many of his remonstrances were commendable.
translations.idiomatic: Hong served long in the Military Section and many of his memorials were praised.

sentences.zh: 削籍後，復罰米二百石輸宣府。

translations.literal: After being struck from the rolls he was again fined two hundred piculs of grain payable to Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: After expulsion he was fined two hundred piculs of grain payable to Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 後起官，終福建左參政。

translations.literal: He was later reappointed and ended as left assistant administration commissioner in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was later reappointed and ended as left assistant administration commissioner in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 葛嵩，字鐘甫，無錫人。

translations.literal: Ge Song, styled Zhongfu, was a native of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Song, courtesy name Zhongfu, came from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年進士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twelfth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 由行人擢禮科給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted from courier to supervising secretary of the Rites Section.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted from courier, he became supervising secretary of the Rites Section.

sentences.zh: 閱薊州軍儲，核貴戚所侵地，歸之民。

translations.literal: He inspected military stores at Jizhou, verified land seized by imperial kin, and returned it to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting Jizhou military stores, he verified lands seized by imperial relatives and restored them to commoners.

sentences.zh: 正德初，以厘營弊力抗權幸。

translations.literal: Early in Zhengde, in reforming camp abuses he forcefully resisted powerful favorites.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengde he fought camp abuses and boldly resisted powerful favorites.

sentences.zh: 請出先朝宮人，諫射獵，因劾魏國公徐俌。

translations.literal: He asked that palace women of the previous reign be released, remonstrated against hunting, and impeached Xu Fu, Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He urged release of palace women from the previous reign, remonstrated against hunting, and impeached Xu Fu, Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 又偕九卿請誅劉瑾。

translations.literal: Together with the Nine Ministers he also asked that Liu Jin be executed.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Nine Ministers in calling for Liu Jin's execution.

sentences.zh: 瑾怒，斥為奸黨，罷歸。

translations.literal: Jin was enraged, branded him a traitor, and sent him home in disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was furious, labeled him a traitor, and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 趙佑，字汝翼，雙流人。

translations.literal: Zhao You, styled Ruyi, was a native of Shuangliu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao You, courtesy name Ruyi, came from Shuangliu.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年進士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twelfth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 由繁昌知縣召為御史。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Fanchang he was summoned to be a censor.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned from magistrate of Fanchang, he became a censor.

sentences.zh: 正德元年六月，災異求言，佑上言：「太監劉瑾、丘聚、馬永成輩日獻鷹犬，導騎射，萬一有銜橛之變，豈不為兩宮憂？

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Zhengde, when calamities prompted calls for advice, You memorialized: "Eunuchs Liu Jin, Qiu Ju, Ma Yongcheng, and their like daily present hawks and hounds and lead Your Majesty in riding and shooting; if there should be a mishap with the bridle, would this not grieve the two palaces?
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Zhengde's first year, when omens prompted open counsel, You wrote: "Eunuchs Liu Jin, Qiu Ju, Ma Yongcheng, and the rest daily offer hawks and hounds and lead Your Majesty in riding and archery; should the reins fail, would this not trouble the two palaces?

sentences.zh: 鎮守內臣鄧原、麥秀頗簡靜，而劉璟、梁裕擠代之。

translations.literal: Garrison eunuchs Deng Yuan and Mai Xiu were rather restrained, yet Liu Jing and Liang Yu crowded them out and replaced them.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison eunuchs Deng Yuan and Mai Xiu had been relatively restrained, yet Liu Jing and Liang Yu displaced them.

sentences.zh: 戶部議馬房草場召民佃種，寧瑾竟自奏止。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue proposed leasing the stud-farm pastures to commoners; Ning and Jin themselves memorialized to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue proposed leasing stud pastures to farmers; Jin himself memorialized to block it.

sentences.zh: 李興擅伐陵木，已坐大辟，乃欲賂左右祈免。

translations.literal: Li Xing illegally cut timber from imperial tombs and already deserved death, yet sought to bribe those close to the throne for pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xing had illegally felled tomb timber and deserved death, yet tried to bribe court intimates for release.

sentences.zh: 他如南京守備劉雲，倉場監督趙忠、韋雋、段循，俱夤緣增設。

translations.literal: Others such as Nanjing commandant Liu Yun and granary supervisors Zhao Zhong, Wei Juan, and Duan Xun were all added through connections.
translations.idiomatic: Others—Nanjing commandant Liu Yun and granary supervisors Zhao Zhong, Wei Juan, and Duan Xun—were all added through patronage.

sentences.zh: 乞置瑾等於法，罷璟、裕毋遣，而汰革額外冗員。

translations.literal: I beg that Jin and his like be punished by law, that Jing and Yu not be sent out, and that supernumerary posts be cut.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Jin and his associates be punished, that Jing and Yu not be dispatched, and extra posts be eliminated.

sentences.zh: 自今政事必諮大臣、臺諫，不為近習所搖，則災變自弭。」

translations.literal: From now on let policy be referred to great ministers and the censorate, not swayed by intimates, and calamities will cease of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: If hereafter policy is referred to ministers and censors and not swayed by favorites, omens will subside of themselves.

sentences.zh: 奏入，群奄大恨。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the eunuch faction hated him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the eunuchs hated him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 帝將大婚，詔取太倉銀四十萬兩。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to marry and ordered four hundred thousand taels taken from the Grand Canal treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to wed and ordered four hundred thousand taels from the Grand Canal treasury.

sentences.zh: 佑言：「左右以婚禮為名，將肆無厭之欲。

translations.literal: You said: "Those around Your Majesty use the wedding as a pretext to indulge boundless desires.
translations.idiomatic: You wrote: "Those around the throne use the wedding as a pretext for boundless spending.

sentences.zh: 計臣懼禍而不敢阻，閣臣避怨而不敢爭。

translations.literal: The planners fear disaster and dare not obstruct; the Grand Secretaries avoid blame and dare not contend.
translations.idiomatic: Planners fear reprisal and dare not object; Grand Secretaries avoid conflict and dare not argue.

sentences.zh: 用如泥沙，坐致耗國。

translations.literal: Funds are spent like sand and the state is drained.
translations.idiomatic: Money is spent like sand and the state is exhausted.

sentences.zh: 不幸興師旅，遘饑饉，將何以為計哉？」

translations.literal: If war should arise or famine strike, what plan will there be?
translations.idiomatic: If war or famine comes, what recourse will there be?

sentences.zh: 九月，宛平郊外李花盛開，佑言：「此陰擅陽權，非偶然也。」

translations.literal: In the ninth month plum blossoms flourished outside Wanping; You said: "This is yin usurping yang—not accidental."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month plum blossomed outside Wanping; You said: "Yin is usurping yang—this is no accident."

sentences.zh: 帝皆不納。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted none of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected all of it.

sentences.zh: 是時，中官益橫，佑與同官朱廷聲、徐鈺交章極論。

translations.literal: At this time eunuchs grew more arrogant; You and his colleagues Zhu Tingsheng and Xu Yu submitted memorials in fierce debate.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs grew bolder; You, Zhu Tingsheng, and Xu Yu submitted fierce joint memorials.

sentences.zh: 章下閣議，將重罪中官。

translations.literal: The memorials went to the Grand Secretariat for discussion and eunuchs were to be heavily punished.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials went to the Grand Secretariat, which was to punish eunuchs severely.

sentences.zh: 事忽中變，劉健、謝遷去位。

translations.literal: Matters suddenly changed; Liu Jian and Xie Qian left office.
translations.idiomatic: Events suddenly shifted; Liu Jian and Xie Qian resigned.

sentences.zh: 瑾遂大逐廷臣忤己者，指佑與廷聲、鈺及陳琳、潘鏜等為奸黨，勒罷之。

translations.literal: Jin then drove out courtiers who opposed him, naming You, Tingsheng, Yu, Chen Lin, Pan Tang, and others as traitors and forcing their dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Jin expelled opposing officials, branding You, Tingsheng, Yu, Chen Lin, Pan Tang, and others traitors and forcing them out.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，佑用薦起山西僉事。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, You was recommended and appointed assistant commissioner in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's fall You was recommended and appointed assistant commissioner in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 朱廷聲，字克諧，進賢人。

translations.literal: Zhu Tingsheng, styled Kexie, was a native of Jinxian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tingsheng, courtesy name Kexie, came from Jinxian.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年進士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twelfth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，終刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign he ended as vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiajing he rose to vice minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 徐鈺，字用礪，江夏人。

translations.literal: Xu Yu, styled Yongli, was a native of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yu, courtesy name Yongli, came from Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士，終四川左布政使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi and ended as left administration commissioner in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi in the ninth year of Hongzhi and ended as left administration commissioner in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 陳琳，字玉疇，甫田人。

translations.literal: Chen Lin, styled Yuchou, was a native of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Lin, courtesy name Yuchou, came from Putian.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the ninth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士改御史，上端本修政十五事。

translations.literal: From Hanlin academician he was changed to censor and submitted fifteen items on restoring fundamental governance.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred from Hanlin academician to censor, he submitted fifteen reforms for restoring fundamental governance.

sentences.zh: 出督南畿學政。

translations.literal: He went out to supervise education in the southern capital region.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to supervise education in the southern capital region.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾逐健、遷，逮戴銑、陸昆等，琳抗章言：「南京窮冬雷震，正旦日食。

translations.literal: When Liu Jin drove out Jian and Qian and arrested Dai Xian and Lu Kun, Lin submitted a defiant memorial: "Nanjing had thunder in deep winter and a solar eclipse on New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin expelled Jian and Qian and arrested Dai Xian and Lu Kun, Lin protested: "Nanjing had winter thunder and a New Year eclipse.

sentences.zh: 正宜修德弭災，委心元寮，博采忠言。

translations.literal: This is the time to cultivate virtue and quell disaster, entrust affairs to senior ministers, and gather loyal counsel broadly.
translations.idiomatic: Now is the time to cultivate virtue, trust senior ministers, and gather loyal counsel.

sentences.zh: 豈宜自棄股肱、隔塞耳目？」

translations.literal: How can Your Majesty abandon your arms and legs and block your eyes and ears?
translations.idiomatic: How can Your Majesty cast aside your chief ministers and seal off your ears and eyes?

sentences.zh: 瑾大怒，謫揭陽丞。

translations.literal: Jin was furious and demoted him to assistant magistrate of Jieyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was enraged and demoted him to assistant magistrate of Jieyang.

sentences.zh: 瑾敗，遷嘉興同知。

translations.literal: When Jin fell, he was transferred to vice prefect of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's fall he was made vice prefect of Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，終南京兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Under Shizong he ended as vice minister of War at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizong he ended as vice minister of War at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 潘鏜，字宗節，六安人。

translations.literal: Pan Tang, styled Zongjie, was a native of Lu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Tang, courtesy name Zongjie, came from Lu'an.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the ninth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 有孝行。

translations.literal: He was noted for filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 為滿城知縣，憂歸。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Mancheng he returned home in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Mancheng he left office to mourn his parents.

sentences.zh: 繼知滑縣，擢御史，陳時務大計四事。

translations.literal: He later governed Huaxian, was promoted to censor, and set forth four great policies of the time.
translations.idiomatic: He later governed Huaxian, became censor, and proposed four major policies.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: Xiaozong praised and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong approved them.

sentences.zh: 正德初，以論高鳳為中人所惡，傳旨鏜黨太監王嶽，除其名。

translations.literal: Early in Zhengde, for criticizing Gao Feng he was hated by eunuchs; an edict was transmitted that Tang was party to eunuch Wang Yue, and his name was removed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengde, criticizing Gao Feng earned eunuch hatred; an edict linked him with Wang Yue and struck his name from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 八年起廣東僉事，謝病歸。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed assistant commissioner in Guangdong but resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed in Guangdong but resigned ill.

sentences.zh: 戴銑，字寶之，婺源人。

translations.literal: Dai Xian, styled Baozhi, was a native of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Xian, courtesy name Baozhi, came from Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士，改庶吉士，授兵科給事中，數有建白。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi, became a Hanlin academician, and was appointed supervising secretary of the Military Section, where he often offered proposals.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi in the ninth year of Hongzhi, entered the Hanlin, and became supervising secretary of the Military Section with many proposals.

sentences.zh: 久之，以便養調南京戶科。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to the Household Section in Nanjing to care for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Later he transferred to the Nanjing Household Section to support his parents.

sentences.zh: 武宗嗣位，偕同官請敕六科檢詳弘治間所行進賢、退奸、節財、訓兵、重祀、慎刑、救災、恤困諸大政，備錄進覽，凡裁決機務悉以為準。

translations.literal: When Wuzong succeeded, he and his colleagues asked that the Six Sections review and record the great policies of the Hongzhi reign—promoting the worthy, removing the wicked, saving funds, training troops, honoring sacrifice, cautious punishment, relieving disaster, and aiding the distressed—for the emperor's review, and that all decisions follow them.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong succeeded, he asked the Six Sections to compile Hongzhi policies on promoting worthies, removing villains, saving funds, training troops, honoring rites, cautious punishment, and disaster relief as standards for governance.

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: The court noted receipt.
translations.idiomatic: The court acknowledged the request.

sentences.zh: 逾月，言四方歲辦多非土產，勞費滋甚，宜蠲其所無。

translations.literal: After a month he said that many annual levies from the regions were not local products and the labor and expense grew worse; what the regions lacked should be exempted.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he argued that many tribute items were not local products and levies should be cut where goods were unavailable.

sentences.zh: 又請勤禦經筵，俾密勿大臣從容獻納。

translations.literal: He also asked that the emperor diligently attend the classics lectures and let confidential ministers offer counsel at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged regular attendance at the classics lectures and leisurely counsel from trusted ministers.

sentences.zh: 既乃與給事中李光翰、徐蕃、牧相、任惠、徐暹及御史薄彥徽等連章奏留劉健、謝遷，且劾中官高鳳。

translations.literal: Then together with supervising secretaries Li Guanghan, Xu Fan, Mu Xiang, Ren Hui, and Xu Xian and censor Bo Yanhui he submitted successive memorials to retain Liu Jian and Xie Qian and impeach the eunuch Gao Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Then with Li Guanghan, Xu Fan, Mu Xiang, Ren Hui, Xu Xian, and censor Bo Yanhui he memorialized to keep Liu Jian and Xie Qian and impeach Gao Feng.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，逮系詔獄，廷杖除名。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, had them arrested and imprisoned, and beaten at court and expelled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, imprisoned them, beat them at court, and expelled them.

sentences.zh: 銑創甚，遂卒。

translations.literal: Xian was badly injured and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was gravely injured and soon died.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，追贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong posthumously made him Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 李光翰，新鄉人。

translations.literal: Li Guanghan was a native of Xinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guanghan came from Xinxiang.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年進士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twelfth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 授南京戶科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary of the Household Section in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Nanjing supervising secretary of the Household Section.

sentences.zh: 正德改元，災異求言。

translations.literal: At the change to Zhengde, calamities prompted calls for advice.
translations.idiomatic: At the Zhengde change, omens prompted open counsel.

sentences.zh: 光翰偕同官疏劾太監苗逵、高鳳、李榮及保國公朱暉，且言大學士劉健等疏陳鹽法事，留中不報，將使老臣不安其位。

translations.literal: Guanghan and his colleagues memorialized against eunuchs Miao Kui, Gao Feng, and Li Rong and the Defender of the State Zhu Hui, and said that Grand Secretary Liu Jian's memorial on the salt laws was held at court without response, which would unsettle old ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Guanghan and colleagues impeached eunuchs Miao Kui, Gao Feng, and Li Rong and Defender Zhu Hui, and noted Liu Jian's salt memorial was withheld, unsettling senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 帝不省。

translations.literal: The emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored them.

sentences.zh: 既削籍歸，後起臺州知府，與蕃同舉治行卓異，尋卒。

translations.literal: After expulsion he was later appointed prefect of Taizhou; he and Xu Fan were both noted for outstanding governance, and he soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Expelled, he later became prefect of Taizhou; he and Xu Fan were praised for governance, then he died.

sentences.zh: 徐蕃，泰州人。

translations.literal: Xu Fan was a native of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fan came from Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年進士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 授南京禮科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary of the Rites Section in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He became Nanjing supervising secretary of the Rites Section.

sentences.zh: 武宗嗣位，復先朝所汰諸冗費，蕃等力爭，不納。

translations.literal: When Wuzong succeeded, redundant expenses cut under the previous reign were restored; Fan and others fought hard but were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong succeeded, Hongzhi cuts were reversed; Fan fought in vain.

sentences.zh: 後起江西參議，從都御史陳金討平東鄉寇。

translations.literal: He was later appointed administration commissioner in Jiangxi and followed Censor-in-Chief Chen Jin in pacifying bandits in Dongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in Jiangxi and followed Chen Jin in pacifying Dongxiang bandits.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖時，累官工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Under Jiajing he rose to vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiajing he rose to vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 任惠，灤州人。

translations.literal: Ren Hui was a native of Luanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Hui came from Luanzhou.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the ninth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 由行人擢南京吏科給事中。

translations.literal: From courier he was promoted to supervising secretary of the Personnel Section in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: From courier he became Nanjing supervising secretary of the Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: 正德元年九月，偕同官諫佚遊，語切直。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Zhengde he and his colleagues remonstrated against idle travel in blunt language.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Zhengde's first year he bluntly remonstrated against idle travel.

sentences.zh: 後起山東僉事，未任卒。

translations.literal: He was later appointed assistant commissioner in Shandong but died before taking office.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed in Shandong but died before assuming post.

sentences.zh: 徐暹，歷城人。

translations.literal: Xu Xian was a native of Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xian came from Licheng.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifteenth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，擢南京工科給事中。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne he was promoted to supervising secretary of the Works Section in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong ascended he became Nanjing supervising secretary of the Works Section.

sentences.zh: 正德改元，因災異上言七事，且請斥英國公張懋、尚書張昇等，撤諸添註內官，明正張瑜、劉文泰用藥失宜致誤先帝，及太監李興擅伐陵木，新寧伯譚佑、侍郎李鐩同事不舉之罪。

translations.literal: At the change to Zhengde, responding to calamities he set forth seven items and asked dismissal of the Duke of Ying Zhang Mao, Minister Zhang Sheng, and others, withdrawal of added eunuchs, clear punishment of Zhang Yu and Liu Wentai for improper medicine that harmed the late emperor, and punishment of eunuch Li Xing for illegal tomb timber, Baron Tan You, and Vice Minister Li Tang for failing to report.
translations.idiomatic: At the Zhengde change he listed seven reforms, demanded dismissal of Zhang Mao, Duke of Ying, Zhang Sheng, and added eunuchs, and prosecution of Zhang Yu, Liu Wentai, Li Xing, Tan You, and Li Tang.

sentences.zh: 帝下之所司。

translations.literal: The emperor referred the matter to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor referred the memorial to the agencies.

sentences.zh: 後起山西僉事，進副使。

translations.literal: He was later appointed assistant commissioner in Shanxi and promoted to vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in Shanxi and was promoted to vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 平巨盜混天王，民德之。

translations.literal: He pacified the great bandit Hun Tianwang and the people honored him.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed the bandit Hun Tianwang and won popular gratitude.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 陸昆，字如玉，歸安人。

translations.literal: Lu Kun, styled Ruyu, was a native of Gui'an.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kun, courtesy name Ruyu, came from Gui'an.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the ninth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 授清豐知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Qingfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Qingfeng.

sentences.zh: 以廉幹征，擢南京御史。

translations.literal: Summoned for integrity and capability, he was promoted to censor in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Recognized for integrity, he was promoted to Nanjing censor.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，疏陳重風紀八事：一，獎直言。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne he memorialized on eight matters to strengthen discipline: first, reward blunt counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong ascended he memorialized eight reforms to strengthen discipline: first, reward blunt counsel.

sentences.zh: 古者，臣下不匡，其刑墨。

translations.literal: In antiquity, if ministers did not correct faults, they were tattooed.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity ministers who failed to correct faults were tattooed.

sentences.zh: 宋制，御史入臺，逾十旬無言，有辱臺之罰。

translations.literal: Under Song rule, when a censor entered the bureau, if he spoke nothing for more than ten weeks he suffered disgrace to the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song rule a censor who spoke nothing for ten weeks was shamed.

sentences.zh: 今郎署建言，如李夢陽、楊子器輩，當加旌擢，而言官考績，宜以章疏多寡及當否為殿最。

translations.literal: Now officials in departments offer counsel, such as Li Mengyang and Yang Ziqi; they should be honored, and censors' evaluations should rank them by the number and merit of their memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Today officials like Li Mengyang and Yang Ziqi should be honored, and censors ranked by memorial quantity and merit.

sentences.zh: 二，復面劾。

translations.literal: Second, restore face-to-face impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Second, restore face-to-face impeachment.

sentences.zh: 舊制，御史上殿，被劾者趨出待罪，即唐人對仗讀彈文遺意。

translations.literal: Under the old practice, when censors entered the hall, the impeached hurried out to await punishment—this preserved the Tang practice of reading impeachment memorials in formal parallel prose.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old practice, censors presented impeachments in court and the accused were made to withdraw and await judgment—preserving the Tang custom of reading charges in formal parallel prose.

sentences.zh: 近率封章奏聞，批答未行，彌縫先入。

translations.literal: Lately memorials are routinely sealed and submitted; before imperial responses are issued, patch-ups are put in place first.
translations.idiomatic: Lately memorials are routinely sealed and submitted, and before the emperor's reply arrives, cover-ups are already underway.

sentences.zh: 乞遵舊典面奏，立取睿裁。

translations.literal: I beg that the old practice of face-to-face presentation be followed, with immediate imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the old practice of face-to-face presentation be restored, with immediate imperial judgment.

sentences.zh: 三，明淑慝。

translations.literal: Third, make good and evil clear.
translations.idiomatic: Third, distinguish the worthy from the wicked.

sentences.zh: 尚書劉大夏、王軾以病乞休；

translations.literal: Ministers Liu Daxia and Wang Shi asked to retire on grounds of illness;
translations.idiomatic: Ministers Liu Daxia and Wang Shi sought retirement on grounds of illness;

sentences.zh: 侍郎張元禎、陳清屢劾不去。

translations.literal: Vice ministers Zhang Yuanzhen and Chen Qing, repeatedly impeached, refuse to leave.
translations.idiomatic: while Vice Ministers Zhang Yuanzhen and Chen Qing, though repeatedly impeached, refuse to go.

sentences.zh: 賢不肖倒置，實治亂消長之關。

translations.literal: The worthy and unworthy are reversed—this truly bears on whether order rises or falls.
translations.idiomatic: The worthy and the unworthy are reversed—a matter that truly governs whether order rises or falls.

sentences.zh: 宜勉留二人，放元禎等還田裏。

translations.literal: The two [ministers] should be urged to remain; Yuanzhen and the others should be released to return to their fields.
translations.idiomatic: The two ministers should be urged to stay, and Yuanzhen and the others should be sent back to their fields.

sentences.zh: 四，核命令。

translations.literal: Fourth, verify orders.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, verify imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 近者言妨左右，頻見留中。

translations.literal: Lately when words hinder those at the emperor's side, they are frequently held at court.
translations.idiomatic: Lately when words offend those at the emperor's side, memorials are frequently withheld at court.

sentences.zh: 事涉所私，輒收成命。

translations.literal: When matters touch private interests, completed orders are promptly rescinded.
translations.idiomatic: When matters touch private interests, completed orders are promptly revoked.

sentences.zh: 乞令諸曹章奏俱具數送閣，已行者得考稽，未行者易奏請。

translations.literal: I beg that all bureau memorials be numbered and sent to the Grand Secretariat; those already enacted may be audited, and those not yet enacted may easily be resubmitted.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that all bureau memorials be numbered and forwarded to the Grand Secretariat so that enacted orders may be audited and pending ones easily resubmitted.

sentences.zh: 五，養銳氣。

translations.literal: Fifth, nurture sharp resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, nurture censorial resolve.

sentences.zh: 御史與都御史，例得互相糾繩，行事不宜牽制。

translations.literal: Censors and the chief censor may by precedent impeach one another; their actions should not be constrained.
translations.idiomatic: Censors and the chief censor may by precedent impeach one another, and their work should not be constrained.

sentences.zh: 六，均差遣。

translations.literal: Sixth, equalize assignments.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, equalize assignments.

sentences.zh: 御史以南北為限，顯分重輕。

translations.literal: Censors are divided by north and south, clearly marking heavy and light.
translations.idiomatic: Censors are divided between north and south, plainly marking one as weightier than the other.

sentences.zh: 自今除巡按面命外，其他差遣及遷轉資格，宜均擬上請，以示一體。

translations.literal: From now on, aside from face-to-face appointments as touring inspectors, other assignments and promotion qualifications should be uniformly submitted for approval, to show equality.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, aside from face-to-face appointments as touring inspectors, other assignments and promotion criteria should be submitted uniformly for approval, to show equal treatment.

sentences.zh: 七，專委任。

translations.literal: Seventh, assign dedicated responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, assign dedicated responsibility.

sentences.zh: 河南道有考核之責，請擇人專任。

translations.literal: The Henan circuit has responsibility for evaluations; I ask that someone be selected for sole charge.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan circuit bears responsibility for evaluations; I ask that a dedicated officer be chosen for the task.

sentences.zh: 八，勵庶官。

translations.literal: Eighth, encourage ordinary officials.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, encourage ordinary officials.

sentences.zh: 郎中田巖、姚汀、張憲，員外郎李承勛、胡世寧、張嵿、顧璘等二十人，皆宜顯擢。

translations.literal: Directors Tian Yan, Yao Ding, and Zhang Xian; vice directors Li Chengxun, Hu Shining, Zhang Ding, and Gu Lin, and twenty others—all should be visibly promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Directors Tian Yan, Yao Ding, and Zhang Xian; Vice Directors Li Chengxun, Hu Shining, Zhang Ding, and Gu Lin, and twenty others—all deserve visible promotion.

sentences.zh: 章下所司。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 又劾中官高鳳、苗逵、保國公朱暉，因請汰南京增設守備內臣，廣開言路，屏絕宴遊騎射。

translations.literal: He also impeached eunuchs Gao Feng and Miao Kui and Defender of the State Zhu Hui, and asked to eliminate the newly added eunuch garrison commanders at Nanjing, broaden channels for counsel, and banish feasting, roaming, and mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached eunuchs Gao Feng and Miao Kui and Defender of the State Zhu Hui, and asked to cut the newly added eunuch garrison commanders at Nanjing, open channels for counsel, and end feasting, roaming, and mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 帝不能從。

translations.literal: The emperor would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not comply.

sentences.zh: 時「八黨」竊柄，朝政日非。

translations.literal: At the time the "Eight Partisans" seized power, and court governance daily worsened.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the "Eight Partisans" held power in secret, and court governance grew worse by the day.

sentences.zh: 昆偕十三道御史薄彥徽、葛浩、貢安甫、王蕃、史良佐、李熙、任諾、姚學禮、張鳴鳳、蔣欽、曹閔、黃昭道、王弘、蕭乾元等，上疏極諫曰：「自古奸臣欲擅主權，必先蠱其心誌。

translations.literal: Kun together with censors of the thirteen circuits—Bo Yanhui, Ge Hao, Gong Anfu, Wang Fan, Shi Liangzuo, Li Xi, Ren Nuo, Yao Xueli, Zhang Mingfeng, Jiang Qin, Cao Min, Huang Zhaodao, Wang Hong, Xiao Qianyuan, and others—submitted a memorial in fierce remonstrance, saying: "Since antiquity, treacherous ministers wishing to monopolize power have always first bewitched the ruler's mind and will.
translations.idiomatic: Kun joined censors from all thirteen circuits—Bo Yanhui, Ge Hao, Gong Anfu, Wang Fan, Shi Liangzuo, Li Xi, Ren Nuo, Yao Xueli, Zhang Mingfeng, Jiang Qin, Cao Min, Huang Zhaodao, Wang Hong, Xiao Qianyuan, and others—in a fierce joint memorial: "Since antiquity, treacherous ministers seeking to monopolize power have always first bewitched the ruler's mind.

sentences.zh: 如趙高勸二世嚴刑肆誌，以極耳目之娛；

translations.literal: Zhao Gao urged the Second Emperor to impose harsh punishments and indulge his desires, to the limit of sensory pleasure;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gao urged the Second Emperor to impose harsh punishments and indulge every desire, to the limit of sensory pleasure;

sentences.zh: 和士開說武成毋自勤約，宜及少壯為樂；

translations.literal: He Shikai told Emperor Wucheng not to restrain himself in diligence and frugality, but to enjoy himself while still young and strong;
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai told Emperor Wucheng not to burden himself with diligence and restraint, but to take pleasure while still young and strong;

sentences.zh: 仇士良教其黨以奢靡導君，勿使親近儒生，知前代興亡之故。

translations.literal: Qiu Shiliang taught his faction to lead the ruler into extravagance and not let him draw near Confucian scholars, lest he learn the causes of rise and fall in former ages.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shiliang taught his faction to lead the ruler into extravagance and keep him from Confucian scholars who might teach him why dynasties rose and fell.

sentences.zh: 其君惑之，卒皆受禍。

translations.literal: Their rulers were deluded and in the end all suffered disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Their rulers were deluded, and in the end all met disaster.

sentences.zh: 陛下嗣位以來，天下颙然望治。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty succeeded to the throne, the realm has looked up in hope of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, the realm has looked up in hope of good governance.

sentences.zh: 乃未幾，寵幸奄寺，顛覆典刑。

translations.literal: Yet before long eunuchs were favored, overturning established law.
translations.idiomatic: Yet before long eunuchs were favored and established law was overturned.

sentences.zh: 太監馬永成、魏彬、劉瑾、傅興、羅祥、谷大用輩共為蒙蔽，日事宴遊。

translations.literal: Eunuchs Ma Yongcheng, Wei Bin, Liu Jin, Fu Xing, Luo Xiang, Gu Dayong, and their like together deceived him, daily given to feasting and roaming.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs Ma Yongcheng, Wei Bin, Liu Jin, Fu Xing, Luo Xiang, Gu Dayong, and their like deceived him together, daily given to feasting and pleasure.

sentences.zh: 上幹天和，災寢疊告，廷臣屢諫，未蒙省納。

translations.literal: He offended Heaven's harmony; calamities piled one upon another; court ministers remonstrated repeatedly, yet received no heed.
translations.idiomatic: He offended Heaven's harmony; calamities piled one upon another; court ministers remonstrated again and again, yet won no heed.

sentences.zh: 若輩必謂『宮中行樂，何關治亂』，此正奸人欺君之故術也。

translations.literal: That crowd surely says, 'What does pleasure in the palace have to do with order and chaos?'—this is precisely the old trick by which villains deceive their ruler.
translations.idiomatic: That crowd surely says, 'What does pleasure in the palace have to do with order and chaos?'—this is precisely the old trick by which villains deceive their ruler.

sentences.zh: 陛下廣殿細旃，豈知小民窮檐蔀屋風雨之不庇；

translations.literal: Your Majesty in broad halls on fine mats—does he know that common people in poor eaves and patched roofs are unprotected from wind and rain;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty dwells in broad halls on fine mats—does he know that common people in patched eaves and broken roofs have no shelter from wind and rain;

sentences.zh: 錦衣玉食，豈知小民祁寒暑雨凍餒之弗堪；

translations.literal: in brocade robes and jade fare—does he know that common people cannot endure scorching heat, bitter cold, driving rain, and hunger;
translations.idiomatic: in brocade robes and jade fare—does he know that common people cannot endure scorching heat, bitter cold, driving rain, and hunger;

sentences.zh: 馳騁宴樂，豈知小民疾首蹙頞赴訴之無路。

translations.literal: galloping in feasting and pleasure—does he know that common people, wracked with grief and furrowed brows, have no road by which to bring their grievances?
translations.idiomatic: galloping in feasting and pleasure—does he know that common people, wracked with grief and furrowed brows, have no way to bring their grievances?

sentences.zh: 昨日雷震郊壇，彗出紫微，夏秋亢旱，江南米價騰貴，京城盜賊橫行。

translations.literal: Yesterday thunder shook the suburban altar; a comet appeared from the Purple Palace; drought raged through summer and autumn; rice prices soared in Jiangnan; bandits ran rampant in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday thunder shook the suburban altar; a comet appeared from the Purple Palace; drought raged through summer and autumn; rice prices soared in Jiangnan; and bandits ran rampant in the capital.

sentences.zh: 可恣情縱欲，不一顧念乎？

translations.literal: Can Your Majesty indulge his desires without a single thought for these things?
translations.idiomatic: Can Your Majesty indulge every desire without a single thought for these things?

sentences.zh: 閣部大臣受顧命之寄，宜隨事匡救，弘濟艱難，言之不聽，必伏闕死諫，以悟聖意。

translations.literal: Grand secretaries and ministers entrusted with the late emperor's charge should rectify affairs as they arise and broadly relieve hardship; if their words are not heeded, they must prostrate themselves at the palace gate and die remonstrating, to awaken the sacred mind.
translations.idiomatic: Grand secretaries and ministers entrusted with the late emperor's charge should set things right as they arise and relieve hardship; if their words go unheeded, they should prostrate themselves at the palace gate and die remonstrating, to awaken the sacred mind.

sentences.zh: 顧乃怠緩悅從，巽順退托。

translations.literal: Yet they are slack and slow, pleased to comply, yielding and retreating behind excuses.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they are slack and slow, pleased to comply, yielding and hiding behind excuses.

sentences.zh: 自為謀則善矣，如先帝付委、天下屬望何？

translations.literal: For their own sake this may be well enough—but what of the late emperor's charge and the realm's hopes?
translations.idiomatic: For their own sake this may be well enough—but what of the late emperor's charge and the realm's hopes?

sentences.zh: 伏望側身修行，亟屏永成輩以絕禍端，委任大臣，務學親政，以還至治。」

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will turn inward and cultivate himself, swiftly remove Yongcheng and his like to cut off the source of disaster, entrust affairs to great ministers, devote himself to learning and personal rule, and restore supreme governance.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope Your Majesty will turn inward and reform himself, swiftly remove Yongcheng and his like to cut off disaster at its root, entrust affairs to great ministers, devote himself to learning and personal rule, and restore supreme governance.

sentences.zh: 疏至，朝事已變，劉健、謝遷皆被逐。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, court affairs had already changed; Liu Jian and Xie Qian had both been driven out.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, court affairs had already changed—Liu Jian and Xie Qian had both been driven out.

sentences.zh: 於是彥徽為首，復上公疏，請留健、遷，而罪永成、瑾等。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yanhui took the lead and again submitted a joint memorial asking that Jian and Qian be retained and that Yongcheng, Jin, and the others be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yanhui took the lead in another joint memorial asking that Jian and Qian be retained and Yongcheng, Jin, and the others be punished.

sentences.zh: 瑾怒，悉逮下詔獄，各杖三十，除名。

translations.literal: Jin in anger had them all arrested and sent to the imperial prison; each was beaten thirty strokes and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Jin in anger had them all arrested and sent to the imperial prison; each received thirty strokes of the rod and was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 昭道、弘、乾元逮捕未至，命即南京闕下杖之。

translations.literal: Zhaodao, Hong, and Qianyuan had not yet been arrested and brought in; they were ordered beaten immediately below the Nanjing palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhaodao, Hong, and Qianyuan had not yet been brought in, they were ordered beaten below the Nanjing palace gate.

sentences.zh: 江西清軍御史王良臣聞昆等被逮，馳疏救，並逮下詔獄，杖三十，斥為民。

translations.literal: Wang Liangchen, the Jiangxi censor overseeing military affairs, hearing that Kun and the others had been arrested, rushed a memorial to save them; he too was arrested and sent to the imperial prison, beaten thirty strokes, and expelled as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Liangchen, the Jiangxi censor overseeing military affairs, hearing that Kun and the others had been arrested, rushed a memorial to save them; he too was sent to the imperial prison, beaten thirty strokes, and expelled as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 後列奸黨五十三人，昆、彥徽等並與焉。

translations.literal: Later a list of fifty-three treacherous partisans was drawn up; Kun, Yanhui, and the others were all included.
translations.idiomatic: Later a list of fifty-three treacherous partisans was drawn up, and Kun, Yanhui, and the others were all included.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，復昆官致仕。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, Kun's office was restored and he retired.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was executed, Kun's office was restored and he retired.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，起用，未行而卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign he was recalled to office but died before taking up the post.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shizong's reign he was recalled to office but died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 薄彥徽，陽曲人。

translations.literal: Bo Yanhui was a native of Yangqu.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Yanhui came from Yangqu.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the ninth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 授四川道御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed censor of the Sichuan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed censor of the Sichuan circuit.

sentences.zh: 嘗劾崔誌端以羽士玷春卿，有直聲。

translations.literal: He once impeached Cui Zhiduan for letting a Taoist priest defile the office of Director of Rites, and won a reputation for bluntness.
translations.idiomatic: He once impeached Cui Zhiduan for letting a Taoist priest defile the office of Director of Rites and won a reputation for bluntness.

sentences.zh: 至是，被杖歸，未及起官卒。

translations.literal: On this occasion he was beaten and sent home; before he could be recalled to office he died.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion he was beaten and sent home; before he could be recalled to office he died.

sentences.zh: 葛浩，字天宏，上虞人。

translations.literal: Ge Hao, styled Tianhong, was a native of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hao, courtesy name Tianhong, came from Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the ninth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 由五河知縣擢御史，數陳時政闕失，孝宗多采納。

translations.literal: Promoted from magistrate of Wuhe to censor, he repeatedly set forth current policy failures, and Xiaozong often adopted his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted from magistrate of Wuhe to censor, he repeatedly pointed out failures in current policy, and Xiaozong often adopted his advice.

sentences.zh: 貢安甫，字克仁，江陰人。

translations.literal: Gong Anfu, styled Keren, was a native of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Anfu, courtesy name Keren, came from Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the ninth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 授長垣知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Changyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Changyuan.

sentences.zh: 孝宗時，擢御史，嘗疏劾壽寧侯張鶴齡。

translations.literal: Under Xiaozong he was promoted to censor and once memorialized against Marquis Shouning Zhang Heling.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiaozong he was promoted to censor and once memorialized against Marquis Shouning Zhang Heling.

sentences.zh: 正德初，考功郎楊子器以山陵事下詔獄，安甫疏力救。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde, Merit Evaluation Director Yang Ziqi was sent to the imperial prison over the imperial tomb affair; Anfu memorialized forcefully to save him.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhengde, Merit Evaluation Director Yang Ziqi was sent to the imperial prison over the imperial tomb affair, and Anfu memorialized forcefully to save him.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書劉大夏為中官所扼，謝病去，戶部侍郎陳清遷南京工部尚書，安甫率御史請還大夏而罷清。

translations.literal: Minister of War Liu Daxia, constrained by eunuchs, resigned on grounds of illness; Vice Minister of Revenue Chen Qing was transferred to Minister of Works at Nanjing; Anfu led the censors in asking that Daxia be restored and Qing dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Liu Daxia, constrained by eunuchs, resigned on grounds of illness; Vice Minister of Revenue Chen Qing was transferred to Minister of Works at Nanjing; Anfu led the censors in asking that Daxia be restored and Qing dismissed.

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: Word came back.
translations.idiomatic: Word came back.

sentences.zh: 彥徽等公疏，安甫筆也，瑾知之，故列奸黨以安甫首南御史。

translations.literal: The joint memorial of Yanhui and the others was in Anfu's hand; Jin knew this, so when listing the treacherous faction he placed Anfu first among the southern censors.
translations.idiomatic: The joint memorial of Yanhui and the others was in Anfu's hand; Jin knew this, so when listing the treacherous faction he placed Anfu first among the southern censors.

sentences.zh: 家居十年，終歲不入城市。

translations.literal: He lived at home for ten years and throughout the year never entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home for ten years and never entered the city all year round.

sentences.zh: 後起山東僉事，甫三月，引疾歸。

translations.literal: Later he was recalled as Assistant Administration Commissioner of Shandong; after only three months he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was recalled as Assistant Administration Commissioner of Shandong; after only three months he cited illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 史良佐，字禹臣，亦江陰人。

translations.literal: Shi Liangzuo, styled Yuchen, was also a native of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Liangzuo, courtesy name Yuchen, also came from Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年進士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twelfth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 由行人擢御史。

translations.literal: Promoted from courier to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted from courier to censor.

sentences.zh: 後起雲南副使。

translations.literal: Later he was recalled as Vice Commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was recalled as Vice Commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 平十八寨苗，賜白金文綺。

translations.literal: He pacified the Miao of the Eighteen Stockades and was granted silver and patterned silks.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the Miao of the Eighteen Stockades and was granted silver and patterned silks.

sentences.zh: 浚海田，溉田千頃，滇人頌之。

translations.literal: He dredged coastal fields and irrigated a thousand qing of land; the people of Yunnan praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged coastal fields and irrigated a thousand qing of land; the people of Yunnan praised him.

sentences.zh: 姚學禮，巴人，家京師。

translations.literal: Yao Xueli was a native of Ba and made his home in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xueli came from Ba and made his home in the capital.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年進士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 正德元年，公疏諫佚遊，不納。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde he joined a joint memorial remonstrating against idle roaming; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengde he joined a joint memorial remonstrating against idle roaming; it was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 後起雲南僉事，終參議。

translations.literal: Later he was recalled as Assistant Administration Commissioner of Yunnan and ended as Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was recalled as Assistant Administration Commissioner of Yunnan and ended his career as Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 張鳴鳳，清平人。

translations.literal: Zhang Mingfeng was a native of Qingping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mingfeng came from Qingping.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士，為永康知縣。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the ninth year of Hongzhi, he served as magistrate of Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the ninth year of Hongzhi, he served as magistrate of Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 有政績，擢御史。

translations.literal: Having administrative achievements, he was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: Having distinguished himself in office, he was promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 後起湖廣僉事，進副使，母憂歸，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was recalled as Assistant Administration Commissioner of Huguang, advanced to Vice Commissioner, returned home on his mother's death, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was recalled as Assistant Administration Commissioner of Huguang, advanced to Vice Commissioner, returned home on his mother's death, and died.

sentences.zh: 蔣欽杖死，別有傳。

translations.literal: Jiang Qin was beaten to death; he has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Qin was beaten to death; he has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 曹閔，上海人。

translations.literal: Cao Min was a native of Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Min came from Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士，為沙縣知縣。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the ninth year of Hongzhi, he served as magistrate of Shaxian.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the ninth year of Hongzhi, he served as magistrate of Shaxian.

sentences.zh: 被征，民號泣攀留，累日不得去。

translations.literal: When he was summoned, the people wept and clung to him, and for days he could not leave.
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned, the people wept and clung to him, and for days he could not leave.

sentences.zh: 既與昆等同得罪。

translations.literal: He then suffered punishment together with Kun and the others.
translations.idiomatic: He then suffered punishment together with Kun and the others.

sentences.zh: 後當起官，以養母不出。

translations.literal: Later, when he was due to be recalled to office, he did not go out because he was caring for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he was due to be recalled to office, he declined because he was caring for his mother.

sentences.zh: 母終，枕塊，得寒疾卒。

translations.literal: When his mother died he mourned on a straw pillow, contracted a cold illness, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he mourned on a straw pillow, contracted a cold illness, and died.

sentences.zh: 黃昭道，平江人，弘治十二年進士。

translations.literal: Huang Zhaodao was a native of Pingjiang and a jinshi of the twelfth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zhaodao came from Pingjiang and received his jinshi degree in the twelfth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 後起廣西僉事，再遷雲南參政。

translations.literal: Later he was recalled as Assistant Administration Commissioner of Guangxi and was transferred again to Administration Commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was recalled as Assistant Administration Commissioner of Guangxi and was transferred again to Administration Commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 撫木邦、孟密有功。

translations.literal: He had merit in pacifying Mubang and Mengmi.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in pacifying Mubang and Mengmi.

sentences.zh: 終左布政使。

translations.literal: He ended as Left Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Left Provincial Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 王弘，六合人，弘治六年進士。

translations.literal: Wang Hong was a native of Luhe and a jinshi of the sixth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong came from Luhe and received his jinshi degree in the sixth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 蕭乾元，萬安人，弘治十二年進士。

translations.literal: Xiao Qianyuan was a native of Wan'an and a jinshi of the twelfth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Qianyuan came from Wan'an and received his jinshi degree in the twelfth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 王蕃、任諾鞫獄時，抵不與知，不足載。

translations.literal: Wang Fan and Ren Nuo, when interrogated in prison, adamantly denied knowledge and are not worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fan and Ren Nuo, when interrogated in prison, adamantly denied knowledge and are not worth recording.

sentences.zh: 王良臣，陳州人。

translations.literal: Wang Liangchen was a native of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Liangchen came from Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年進士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 官南京御史。

translations.literal: He served as a censor at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a Nanjing censor.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，起山東副使，終按察使。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, he was recalled as Vice Commissioner of Shandong and ended as Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed, he was recalled as Vice Commissioner of Shandong and ended his career as Surveillance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 蔣欽，字子修，常熟人。

translations.literal: Jiang Qin, styled Zixiu, was a native of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Qin, courtesy name Zixiu, came from Changshu.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the ninth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 授衛輝推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Weihui.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Weihui.

sentences.zh: 征擢南京御史，數有論奏。

translations.literal: Summoned and promoted to Nanjing censor, he repeatedly submitted memorials and critiques.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned and promoted to Nanjing censor, he repeatedly submitted critiques and memorials.

sentences.zh: 正德元年，劉瑾逐大學士劉健、謝遷，欽偕同官薄彥徽等切諫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde, Liu Jin expelled Grand Secretaries Liu Jian and Xie Qian; Qin joined his colleague Bo Yanhui and others in urgent remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengde, Liu Jin expelled Grand Secretaries Liu Jian and Xie Qian; Qin joined his colleague Bo Yanhui and others in urgent remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 瑾大怒，逮下詔獄，廷杖為民。

translations.literal: Jin was furious; they were arrested and sent to the imperial prison, beaten at court, and reduced to commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Jin had them arrested and sent to the imperial prison, beaten at court, and reduced to commoners.

sentences.zh: 居三日，欽獨具疏曰：「劉瑾，小豎耳。

translations.literal: Three days later, Qin alone prepared a memorial, saying: "Liu Jin is but a petty eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later, Qin alone submitted a memorial, saying: "Liu Jin is but a petty eunuch.

sentences.zh: 陛下親以腹心，倚以耳目，待以股肱，殊不知瑾悖逆之徒，蠹國之賊也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty personally treats him as your innermost confidant, relies on him as your eyes and ears, and employs him as your right arm—and yet you do not know that Jin is a rebellious man, a thief who devours the state.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty personally treats him as your innermost confidant, relies on him as your eyes and ears, and employs him as your right arm—yet you do not know that Jin is a rebellious man, a thief who devours the state.

sentences.zh: 忿臣等奏留二輔，抑諸權奸，矯旨逮問，予杖削職。

translations.literal: Angered that we memorialized to keep the two chief ministers and restrain the power-seeking villains, he forged an edict to arrest and interrogate us, had us beaten, and stripped us of office.
translations.idiomatic: Angered that we memorialized to keep the two chief ministers and restrain the power-seeking villains, he forged an edict to arrest and interrogate us, had us beaten, and stripped us of office.

sentences.zh: 然臣思畎畝猶不忘君，況待命衽席，目擊時弊，烏忍不言。

translations.literal: Yet I reflect that even one tilling the fields does not forget his lord; how much more, awaiting orders at my sleeping mat, witnessing present abuses—how can I bear not to speak?
translations.idiomatic: Yet I reflect that even a farmer in the fields does not forget his lord; how much more, lying at my post, witnessing the abuses of the day—how can I bear to stay silent?

sentences.zh: 昨瑾要索天下三司官賄，人千金，甚有至五千金者。

translations.literal: Yesterday Jin demanded bribes from provincial officials throughout the realm—one thousand taels per person, and some as much as five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Only yesterday Jin demanded bribes from provincial officials throughout the realm—a thousand taels per man, and some as much as five thousand.

sentences.zh: 不與則貶斥，與之則遷擢。

translations.literal: Those who refused were demoted and expelled; those who complied were transferred and promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Those who refused were demoted and expelled; those who paid were transferred and promoted.

sentences.zh: 通國皆寒心，而陛下獨用之於左右，是不知左右有賊，而以賊為腹心也。

translations.literal: The whole realm shuddered with dread, yet Your Majesty alone employs him at your side—this means not knowing there is a thief at your side and taking a thief for your innermost confidant.
translations.idiomatic: The whole realm shuddered with dread, yet Your Majesty alone keeps him at your side—you do not see the thief beside you and take a thief for your innermost confidant.

sentences.zh: 給事中劉蒨指陛下暗於用人，昏於行事，而瑾削其秩，撻辱之。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Liu Qian pointed out that Your Majesty is dim in appointing men and muddled in conduct; Jin reduced his rank and beat and humiliated him.
