translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Liu Qian pointed out that Your Majesty is dim in appointing men and muddled in conduct; Jin reduced his rank and beat and humiliated him.

sentences.zh: 矯旨禁諸言官，無得妄生議論。

translations.literal: Forging an edict, he forbade all remonstrating officials from rashly initiating discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Forging an edict, he forbade all remonstrating officials from speaking out of turn.

sentences.zh: 不言則失於坐視，言之則虐以非法。

translations.literal: To remain silent is to fail by sitting and watching; to speak is to be tormented contrary to law.
translations.idiomatic: To remain silent is to fail by sitting and watching; to speak is to be punished unlawfully.

sentences.zh: 通國皆寒心，而陛下獨用之於前後，是不知前後有賊，而以賊為耳目股肱也。

translations.literal: The whole realm shuddered with dread, yet Your Majesty alone employs him before and behind—this means not knowing there is a thief before and behind you and taking a thief for your eyes, ears, and right arm.
translations.idiomatic: The whole realm shuddered with dread, yet Your Majesty alone keeps him before and behind you—you do not see the thief around you and take a thief for your eyes, ears, and right arm.

sentences.zh: 一賊弄權，萬民失望，愁嘆之聲動徹天地。

translations.literal: One villain manipulates power; the myriad people despair; the sound of grief and lamentation shakes heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: One villain wields power; the myriad people despair; grief and lamentation shake heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 陛下顧懵然不聞，縱之使壞天下事，亂祖宗法。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, however, remains oblivious and does not hear, letting him ruin affairs under heaven and overturn the laws of the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, however, remains oblivious and does not hear, letting him ruin affairs under heaven and overturn the laws of the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 陛下尚何以自立乎？

translations.literal: How can Your Majesty still stand on your own?
translations.idiomatic: How can Your Majesty still stand on your own?

sentences.zh: 幸聽臣言，急誅瑾以謝天下，然後殺臣以謝瑾。

translations.literal: I beg you to heed my words: execute Jin at once to answer the realm, and then kill me to answer Jin.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to heed my words: execute Jin at once to answer the realm, and then kill me to answer Jin.

sentences.zh: 使朝廷一正，萬邪不能入；

translations.literal: Let the court be rectified once and ten thousand evils cannot enter;
translations.idiomatic: Let the court be rectified once and ten thousand evils cannot enter;

sentences.zh: 君心一正，萬欲不能侵，臣之願也。

translations.literal: let the ruler's heart be rectified once and ten thousand desires cannot invade—this is my wish.
translations.idiomatic: let the ruler's heart be rectified once and ten thousand desires cannot invade—this is my wish.

sentences.zh: 今日之國家，乃祖宗之國家也。

translations.literal: The state of today is the state of the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: The state of today is the state of the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 陛下茍重祖宗之國家，則聽臣所奏。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly values the ancestral state, then heed what I submit.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly values the ancestral state, then heed what I submit.

sentences.zh: 如其輕之，則任瑾所欺。」

translations.literal: If you treat it lightly, then leave yourself to be deceived by Jin.
translations.idiomatic: If you treat it lightly, then leave yourself to be deceived by Jin.

sentences.zh: 疏入，再杖三十，系獄。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, he was beaten again thirty blows and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, he was beaten thirty blows again and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 越三日，復具疏曰：「臣與賊瑾勢不兩立。

translations.literal: Three days later, he again prepared a memorial, saying: "I and the villain Jin cannot stand together.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later, he again submitted a memorial, saying: "I and the villain Jin cannot stand together.

sentences.zh: 賊瑾蓄惡已非一朝，乘間起釁，乃其本誌。

translations.literal: The villain Jin has harbored evil not for a single morning; seizing an opportunity to stir trouble is his original intent.
translations.idiomatic: The villain Jin has harbored evil not for a single morning; seizing an opportunity to stir trouble is his original intent.

sentences.zh: 陛下日與嬉遊，茫不知悟。

translations.literal: Your Majesty daily disports yourself in pleasure, oblivious and unaware.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty daily disports yourself in pleasure, oblivious and unaware.

sentences.zh: 內外臣庶，凜如冰淵。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners within and without tremble as if on ice above an abyss.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners within and without tremble as if on ice above an abyss.

sentences.zh: 臣昨再疏受杖，血肉淋漓，伏枕獄中，終難自默，願借上方劍斬之。

translations.literal: Yesterday, having twice memorialized and been beaten until flesh and blood streamed, I lie pillow-bound in prison—but I cannot remain silent; I wish to borrow the imperial sword above to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday, having twice memorialized and been beaten until flesh and blood streamed, I lie wounded in prison—yet I cannot remain silent; I wish to borrow the imperial sword above to behead him.

sentences.zh: 朱雲何人，臣肯少讓？

translations.literal: Who was Zhu Yun, that I should yield even slightly?
translations.idiomatic: Who was Zhu Yun, that I should yield even slightly?

sentences.zh: 陛下試將臣較瑾，瑾忠乎，臣忠乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, try comparing me with Jin—is Jin loyal, or am I loyal?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, try comparing me with Jin—is Jin loyal, or am I loyal?

sentences.zh: 忠與不忠，天下皆知之，陛下亦洞然知之，何仇於臣，而信任此逆賊耶？

translations.literal: Loyal or disloyal—the realm all knows it, and Your Majesty knows it clearly too; what grudge do you hold against me that you trust this rebellious villain?
translations.idiomatic: Loyal or disloyal—the realm all knows it, and Your Majesty knows it clearly too; what grudge do you hold against me that you trust this rebellious villain?

sentences.zh: 臣骨肉都銷，涕泗交作，七十二歲老父，不顧養矣。

translations.literal: My flesh and bones are all worn away; tears and mucus run together; my seventy-two-year-old father—I can no longer care for him.
translations.idiomatic: My flesh and bones are all worn away; tears stream down my face; my seventy-two-year-old father—I can no longer care for him.

sentences.zh: 臣死何足惜，但陛下覆國喪家之禍起於旦夕，是大可惜也！

translations.literal: My death is nothing to regret, but the calamity of overturned state and ruined house for Your Majesty may arise overnight—that is what truly deserves regret!
translations.idiomatic: My death is nothing to regret, but the calamity of overturned state and ruined house for Your Majesty may arise overnight—that is what truly deserves regret!

sentences.zh: 陛下誠殺瑾梟之午門，使天下知臣欽有敢諫之直，陛下有誅賊之明。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly kills Jin and displays his head at Meridian Gate, the realm will know that I, Qin, had the rectitude to remonstrate boldly, and Your Majesty had the clarity to execute the villain.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly kills Jin and displays his head at Meridian Gate, the realm will know that I, Qin, had the courage to remonstrate boldly, and Your Majesty had the clarity to execute the villain.

sentences.zh: 陛下不殺此賊，當先殺臣，使臣得與龍逢、比幹同遊地下，臣誠不願與此賊並生。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not kill this villain, you should kill me first, that I may wander the underworld with Long Feng and Bi Gan; I truly do not wish to live together with this villain.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not kill this villain, you should kill me first, that I may join Long Feng and Bi Gan in the underworld; I truly do not wish to live together with this villain.

sentences.zh: 疏入，復杖三十。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, he was beaten again thirty blows.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, he was beaten thirty blows again.

sentences.zh: 方欽屬草時，燈下微聞鬼聲。

translations.literal: When Qin was drafting the memorial, he faintly heard ghostly sounds under the lamp.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin was drafting the memorial, he faintly heard ghostly sounds under the lamp.

sentences.zh: 欽：「念疏上且掇奇禍，此殆先人之靈欲吾寢此奏耳。」

translations.literal: Qin said: "Thinking that once the memorial goes up I shall bring extraordinary calamity, this must be the spirit of my ancestors wanting me to suppress this memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Qin said: "Thinking that once the memorial goes up I shall bring extraordinary calamity, this must be the spirit of my ancestors wanting me to suppress this memorial.

sentences.zh: 因整衣冠立曰：「果先人，盍厲聲以告。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he straightened his robes and cap and stood, saying: "If you are truly my ancestors, why not speak loudly and tell me?
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he straightened his robes and cap and stood, saying: "If you are truly my ancestors, why not speak loudly and tell me?

sentences.zh: 言未已，聲出壁間，益淒愴。

translations.literal: Before he finished speaking, the sound came from within the wall, growing ever more mournful.
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished speaking, the sound came from within the wall, growing ever more mournful.

sentences.zh: 欽嘆曰：「業已委身，義不得顧私，使緘默負國為先人羞，不孝孰甚！」

translations.literal: Qin sighed and said: "Having already committed myself, by duty I cannot look to private ends; to keep silent and fail the state would bring shame on my ancestors—what could be more unfilial!
translations.idiomatic: Qin sighed and said: "Having already committed myself, by duty I cannot look to private ends; to keep silent and fail the state would bring shame on my ancestors—what could be more unfilial!

sentences.zh: 復坐，奮筆曰：「死即死，此稿不可易也！」

translations.literal: He sat again and wrote resolutely: "Die I may, but this draft shall not be changed!
translations.idiomatic: He sat again and wrote resolutely: "Die I may, but this draft shall not be changed!

sentences.zh: 聲遂止。

translations.literal: The sounds then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The sounds then ceased.

sentences.zh: 杖後三日，卒於獄，年四十九。

translations.literal: Three days after the beating, he died in prison at the age of forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Three days after the beating, he died in prison at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, Qin was posthumously given the title Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was executed, Qin was posthumously given the title Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，賜祭葬，錄一子入監。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign, he was granted sacrificial rites and burial honors, and one son was enrolled in the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiajing reign, he was granted sacrificial rites and burial honors, and one son was enrolled in the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 周璽，字天章，廬州衛人。

translations.literal: Zhou Xi, styled Tianzhang, was a native of Luzhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xi, courtesy name Tianzhang, came from Luzhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the ninth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 授吏科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Office of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Office of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 三遷禮科都給事中。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became chief supervising secretary in the Office of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became chief supervising secretary in the Office of Rites.

sentences.zh: 慷慨好言事。

translations.literal: Bold and fond of speaking on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and fond of speaking on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 明年擢順天府丞。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Vice Magistrate of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was promoted to Vice Magistrate of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 璽論諫深切，率與中官牴牾，劉瑾等積不能堪。

translations.literal: Xi's remonstrances were fierce and deep; he repeatedly clashed with eunuchs, and Liu Jin and the rest could not long endure it.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's remonstrances were fierce and penetrating; he repeatedly clashed with eunuchs, and Liu Jin and the rest could not long endure it.

sentences.zh: 至是，命璽與監丞張淮、侍郎張縉、都御史張鸞、錦衣都指揮楊玉勘近縣皇莊。

translations.literal: At this time he was ordered together with Assistant Director Zhang Huai, Vice Minister Zhang Jin, Censor-in-Chief Zhang Luan, and Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard Yang Yu to investigate imperial estates in nearby counties.
translations.idiomatic: At this time he was ordered together with Assistant Director Zhang Huai, Vice Minister Zhang Jin, Censor-in-Chief Zhang Luan, and Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard Yang Yu to investigate imperial estates in nearby counties.

sentences.zh: 玉，瑾黨，三人皆下之。

translations.literal: Yang Yu was a Jin partisan; the other three all deferred to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yu was a Jin partisan; the other three all deferred to him.

sentences.zh: 璽辭色無假，且公移與玉止牒文。

translations.literal: Xi showed no false courtesy in word or bearing, and in official communications to Yu gave only the bare dispatch form.
translations.idiomatic: Xi showed no false courtesy in word or bearing, and in official communications to Yu gave only the bare dispatch form.

sentences.zh: 玉奏璽侮慢敕使，瑾即矯旨逮下詔獄，搒掠死。

translations.literal: Yu memorialized that Xi had insulted the imperial envoy; Jin immediately forged an edict to arrest him and send him to the imperial prison, where he was tortured to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yu memorialized that Xi had insulted the imperial envoy; Jin immediately forged an edict to arrest him and send him to the imperial prison, where he was tortured to death.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，詔復官賜祭，恤其家。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, an edict restored his office, granted sacrificial rites, and provided relief to his family.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was executed, an edict restored his office, granted sacrificial rites, and provided relief to his family.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，錄一子。

translations.literal: At the start of Jiajing, one son was enrolled for office.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jiajing, one son was enrolled for office.

sentences.zh: 又御史塗禎，新淦人也。

translations.literal: There was also censor Tu Zhen, a native of Xingan.
translations.idiomatic: There was also censor Tu Zhen, who came from Xingan.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twelfth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twelfth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 初為江陰知縣。

translations.literal: At first he served as magistrate of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as magistrate of Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 正德初，巡鹽長蘆。

translations.literal: In the early Zhengde reign, he toured the salt administration at Changlu.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhengde reign, he toured the salt administration at Changlu.

sentences.zh: 瑾縱私人中鹽，又命其黨畢真托取海物，侵奪商利，禎皆據法裁之。

translations.literal: Jin allowed his private agents to enter the salt trade, and also had his partisan Bi Zhen use pretexts to seize marine goods and encroach on merchants' profits; Zhen judged all these cases according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Jin allowed his private agents to enter the salt trade, and also had his partisan Bi Zhen use pretexts to seize marine goods and encroach on merchants' profits; Zhen judged all these cases according to law.

sentences.zh: 比還朝，遇瑾止長揖。

translations.literal: When he returned to court and met Jin, he gave only a formal bow with joined hands.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to court and met Jin, he gave only a formal bow with joined hands.

sentences.zh: 瑾怒，矯旨下詔獄。

translations.literal: Jin was angry and forged an edict to send him to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was angry and forged an edict to send him to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 江陰人在都下者，謀斂錢賂瑾解之，禎不可，喟然曰：「死耳，豈以汙父老哉！」

translations.literal: Jiangyin men in the capital plotted to collect money to bribe Jin for his release; Zhen would not allow it, and sighed: "Death is all there is—how could I defile the elders of my home!
translations.idiomatic: Jiangyin men in the capital plotted to collect money to bribe Jin for his release; Zhen would not allow it, and sighed: "Death is all there is—how could I defile the elders of my home!

sentences.zh: 遂杖三十，論戍肅州，創重竟死獄中。

translations.literal: He was beaten thirty blows, sentenced to exile at Suzhou in Gansu, and with wounds grave died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: He was beaten thirty blows, sentenced to exile at Suzhou in Gansu, and with grave wounds died in prison.

sentences.zh: 瑾怒未已，取其子樸補伍。

translations.literal: Jin's anger not yet spent, he seized his son Pu and made him fill a military register.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's anger not yet spent, he seized his son Pu and made him fill a military register.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，樸乃還，禎復官賜祭。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, Pu returned home, and Zhen was posthumously restored to office and granted sacrificial rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was executed, Pu returned home, and Zhen was posthumously restored to office and granted sacrificial rites.

sentences.zh: 湯禮敬，字仁甫，丹徒人。

translations.literal: Tang Lijing, styled Renfu, was a native of Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Lijing, courtesy name Renfu, came from Dantu.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the ninth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the ninth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 授行人，擢刑科給事中。

translations.literal: Appointed courier, then promoted to supervising secretary in the Office of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed courier, then promoted to supervising secretary in the Office of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 正德初，上言：「陛下踐阼以來，上天屢示災譴。

translations.literal: In the early Zhengde reign he submitted: "Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, Heaven has repeatedly shown disasters and reproof.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhengde reign he submitted: "Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, Heaven has repeatedly shown disasters and reproof.

sentences.zh: 不謹天戒，惟走馬射獵，遊樂無度。

translations.literal: Not heeding Heaven's warning, you only gallop horses and hunt, indulging in pleasure without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Not heeding Heaven's warning, you only gallop horses and hunt, indulging in pleasure without limit.

sentences.zh: 頃四月中旬，雷電雨雹，當六陽用事時，陰氣乃與之抗，此幸臣竊權，忠鯁疏遠之應也。」

translations.literal: Recently in mid-April, thunder, lightning, rain, and hail—when the six yang forces should hold sway, yin forces rose against them; this is the response to favored ministers usurping power and loyal, straight-spoken men being kept distant.
translations.idiomatic: Recently in mid-April, thunder, lightning, rain, and hail struck—when the six yang forces should hold sway, yin forces rose against them; this is Heaven's response to favored ministers usurping power and loyal, straight-spoken men being kept at a distance.

sentences.zh: 已，又論兩廣鎮監韋經，又偕九卿伏闕請誅「八黨」。

translations.literal: Thereafter he also criticized Wei Jing, the superintendent of the Guangdong-Guangxi garrison, and together with the Nine Ministers knelt before the palace gate requesting execution of the "Eight Partisans."
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he also criticized Wei Jing, the superintendent of the Guangdong-Guangxi garrison, and together with the Nine Ministers knelt before the palace gate requesting execution of the "Eight Partisans."

sentences.zh: 劉瑾銜之，尋以其請當審奏囚決之日，有訴冤者屏勿奏，指為變祖制，謫薊州判官。

translations.literal: Liu Jin bore a grudge; soon, because on the day for reviewing prisoners and announcing sentences he requested that those appealing injustice be barred from reporting and was charged with altering ancestral institutions, he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin bore a grudge; soon, because on the day for reviewing prisoners and announcing sentences he had requested that those appealing injustice be barred from reporting, he was charged with altering ancestral institutions and demoted to assistant magistrate of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 後列奸黨給事中十六人，禮敬居首，罷歸。

translations.literal: Later, when the sixteen partisan supervising secretaries were listed, Lijing was named first and was dismissed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the sixteen partisan supervising secretaries were listed, Lijing was named first and was dismissed to return home.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 瑾惡言官譏切時政多刺己，輒假他事坐之。

translations.literal: Jin hated that remonstrating officials criticized current policy and often aimed barbs at him; he would always use other pretexts to convict them.
translations.idiomatic: Jin hated that remonstrating officials criticized current policy and often aimed barbs at him; he would always use other pretexts to convict them.

sentences.zh: 禮敬得罪後，有王渙、何紹正。

translations.literal: After Lijing suffered punishment, there were Wang Huan and He Shaozheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Lijing suffered punishment, there were Wang Huan and He Shaozheng.

sentences.zh: 王渙，字時霖，象山人。

translations.literal: Wang Huan, styled Shilin, was a native of Xiangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huan, courtesy name Shilin, came from Xiangshan.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the ninth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the ninth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 由長樂知縣征授御史。

translations.literal: Summoned from magistrate of Changle, he was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned from his post as magistrate of Changle, he was appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 正德元年，應詔條上應天要道五事，語多斥宦官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde, responding to an edict, he listed five essential matters responding to Heaven, his language largely condemning eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengde, responding to an edict, he listed five essential matters responding to Heaven, his language largely condemning eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 明年出視山海諸關，以病謝事未行。

translations.literal: The next year he was sent out to inspect the passes of Shanhai; citing illness he declined the appointment and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was sent out to inspect the passes of Shanhai; citing illness he declined the appointment and did not go.

sentences.zh: 盜發其部內，都御史劉宇承瑾指劾渙失報。

translations.literal: Bandits arose within his jurisdiction; Censor-in-Chief Liu Yu, acting on Jin's direction, impeached Huan for failure to report.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits arose within his jurisdiction; Censor-in-Chief Liu Yu, acting on Jin's direction, impeached Huan for failure to report.

sentences.zh: 逮下詔獄，杖之，斥為民。

translations.literal: He was arrested and sent to the imperial prison, beaten, and reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: He was arrested and sent to the imperial prison, beaten, and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 瑾敗，復官致仕。

translations.literal: When Jin fell, his office was restored and he retired.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin fell, his office was restored and he retired.

sentences.zh: 何紹正，淳安人。

translations.literal: He Shaozheng was a native of Chun'an.
translations.idiomatic: He Shaozheng came from Chun'an.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the fifteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifteenth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed courier.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed courier.

sentences.zh: 正德三年擢吏科給事中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengde he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Office of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhengde he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Office of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 中官廖堂鎮河南，奏保方面數人，且擅擬遷調。

translations.literal: The eunuch Liao Tang, stationed in Henan, memorialized recommending several provincial officials and took it upon himself to propose transfers and appointments.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Liao Tang, stationed in Henan, memorialized recommending several provincial officials and took it upon himself to propose transfers and appointments.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書許進等不能難，紹正劾之。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Xu Jin and the others could not refute him; Shaozheng impeached them.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Xu Jin and the others could not refute him; Shaozheng impeached them.

sentences.zh: 瑾不得已責堂自陳，而心甚銜紹正。

translations.literal: Jin had no choice but to order Tang to submit a self-accusation, but he deeply resented Shaozheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had no choice but to order Tang to submit a self-accusation, but he deeply resented Shaozheng.

sentences.zh: 及冬，坐頒歷導駕失儀，杖之闕下，謫海州判官。

translations.literal: When winter came, Shaozheng was convicted of impropriety while distributing the calendar and guiding the imperial procession; he was beaten beneath the palace gate and demoted to assistant magistrate of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When winter came, Shaozheng was convicted of impropriety while distributing the calendar and guiding the imperial procession; he was beaten beneath the palace gate and demoted to assistant magistrate of Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 屢遷池州知府，築銅陵五十余圩以備旱潦。

translations.literal: After several promotions he became prefect of Chizhou, where he built more than fifty embankments at Tongling to guard against drought and flood.
translations.idiomatic: After several promotions he became prefect of Chizhou, where he built more than fifty embankments at Tongling to guard against drought and flood.

sentences.zh: 宸濠反，攻安慶，池人震恐，紹正登陴固守。

translations.literal: When Chen Hao rebelled and attacked Anqing, the people of Chizhou were terrified; Shaozheng mounted the walls and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Hao rebelled and attacked Anqing, the people of Chizhou were terrified; Shaozheng mounted the walls and held firm.

sentences.zh: 事平，增俸一級，遷江西參政致仕。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, his salary was raised one grade and he was transferred to Jiangxi as administration commissioner before retiring.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, his salary was raised one grade and he was transferred to Jiangxi as administration commissioner before retiring.

sentences.zh: 池人為立祠，與宋包拯並祀。

translations.literal: The people of Chizhou built a shrine for him and worshipped him together with the Song official Bao Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chizhou built a shrine for him and worshipped him together with the Song official Bao Zheng.

sentences.zh: 許天錫，字啟衷，閩縣人。

translations.literal: Xu Tianxi, styled Qizhong, was a native of Min County.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Tianxi, courtesy name Qizhong, came from Min County.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the sixth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 思親成疾，陳情乞假。

translations.literal: Longing for his parents, he fell ill and submitted a petition begging leave.
translations.idiomatic: Longing for his parents, he fell ill and submitted a petition begging leave.

sentences.zh: 孝宗賜傳以行。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong granted him a post horse for the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong granted him a post horse for the journey.

sentences.zh: 還朝，授吏科給事中。

translations.literal: On returning to court he was appointed supervising secretary in the Office of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was appointed supervising secretary in the Office of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時言官何天衢、倪天明與天錫並負時望，都人有「臺省三天」之目。

translations.literal: At the time the remonstrating officials He Tianqu and Ni Tianming, together with Tianxi, all enjoyed great public esteem; the people of the capital spoke of them as the "Three Heavens of the Censorate and Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: At the time the remonstrating officials He Tianqu and Ni Tianming, together with Tianxi, all enjoyed great public esteem; the people of the capital spoke of them as the "Three Heavens of the Censorate and Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 十二年，建安書林火。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, a fire broke out in the publishing quarter of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, a fire broke out in the publishing quarter of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 天錫言：「去歲闕里孔廟災，今茲建安又火，古今書版蕩為灰燼。

translations.literal: Tianxi said: "Last year the Confucian temple at Qufu was destroyed by fire; now Jian'an has burned as well, and printing blocks of books ancient and modern have been reduced to ash.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi said: "Last year the Confucian temple at Qufu was destroyed by fire; now Jian'an has burned as well, and printing blocks of books ancient and modern have been reduced to ash.

sentences.zh: 闕里，道所從出；

translations.literal: Qufu is where the Way has its source;
translations.idiomatic: Qufu is where the Way has its source;

sentences.zh: 書林，文章所萃聚也。

translations.literal: the publishing quarter is where literature gathers.
translations.idiomatic: the publishing quarter is where literature gathers.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》書宣榭火，說者曰：『榭所以藏樂器也。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals records the burning of the Xuan Pavilion; commentators say: 'The pavilion was where musical instruments were stored.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals records the burning of the Xuan Pavilion; commentators say: 'The pavilion was where musical instruments were stored.

sentences.zh: 天意若曰不能行政令，何以禮樂為？

translations.literal: Heaven's intent seems to say: if you cannot administer government and commands, what use is ritual and music?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's intent seems to say: if you cannot administer government and commands, what use is ritual and music?

sentences.zh: 禮樂不行，天故火其藏以戒也。』

translations.literal: When ritual and music are not practiced, Heaven therefore burns their storehouse as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: When ritual and music are not practiced, Heaven therefore burns their storehouse as a warning.

sentences.zh: 頃師儒失職，正教不修。

translations.literal: Recently teachers and scholars have failed in their duties, and orthodox instruction has not been cultivated.
translations.idiomatic: Recently teachers and scholars have failed in their duties, and orthodox instruction has not been cultivated.

sentences.zh: 上之所尚者浮華，下之所習者枝葉。

translations.literal: What those above esteem is mere ornament; what those below practice is leafy branchwork.
translations.idiomatic: What those above esteem is mere ornament; what those below practice is leafy branchwork.

sentences.zh: 此番災變，似欲為儒林一掃積垢。

translations.literal: This calamity seems intended to sweep accumulated filth from the grove of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: This calamity seems intended to sweep accumulated filth from the grove of scholars.

sentences.zh: 宜因此遣官臨視，刊定經史有益之書。

translations.literal: Accordingly, officials should be dispatched to inspect on the spot and publish editions of the classics and histories that are truly useful.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, officials should be dispatched to inspect on the spot and publish editions of the classics and histories that are truly useful.

sentences.zh: 其余晚宋陳言，如論範、論草、策略、策海、文衡、文髓、主意、講章之類，悉行禁刻。

translations.literal: As for the stale formulas of late Song, such as Lunfan, Lungcao, Celue, Cehai, Wenheng, Wensui, Zhuyi, Jiangzhang, and the like, printing of them should be entirely forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: As for the stale formulas of late Song, such as Lunfan, Lungcao, Celue, Cehai, Wenheng, Wensui, Zhuyi, Jiangzhang, and the like, printing of them should be entirely forbidden.

sentences.zh: 其於培養人才，實非淺鮮。」

translations.literal: This would by no means be a small benefit in cultivating talent."
translations.idiomatic: This would by no means be a small benefit in cultivating talent."

sentences.zh: 所司議從其言，就令提學官校勘。

translations.literal: The responsible offices deliberated and accepted his proposal, ordering education commissioners to collate and verify accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices deliberated and accepted his proposal, ordering education commissioners to collate and verify accordingly.

sentences.zh: 大同失事，天錫往核，具得其狀，巡撫洪漢、中官劉雲、總兵官王璽以下鹹獲罪。

translations.literal: When disaster struck at Datong, Tianxi went to investigate and fully established the facts; Grand Coordinator Hong Han, the eunuch Liu Yun, Commander-in-Chief Wang Xi, and others all suffered punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck at Datong, Tianxi went to investigate and fully established the facts; Grand Coordinator Hong Han, the eunuch Liu Yun, Commander-in-Chief Wang Xi, and others all suffered punishment.

sentences.zh: 內使劉雄怒儀真知縣徐淮廚傳不飭，訴之南京守備中官以聞，逮淮系詔獄。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Liu Xiong, angered that Magistrate Xu Huai of Yizhi had not properly provisioned his kitchen, complained to the Nanjing garrison eunuch, who reported it; Huai was arrested and imprisoned in the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: The inner attendant Liu Xiong, angered that Magistrate Xu Huai of Yizhi had not properly provisioned his kitchen, complained to the Nanjing garrison eunuch, who reported it; Huai was arrested and imprisoned in the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 天錫及御史馮允中論救，卒調淮邊縣。

translations.literal: Tianxi and Censor Feng Yunzhong pleaded for his release; in the end Huai was transferred to a border county.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi and Censor Feng Yunzhong pleaded for his release; in the end Huai was transferred to a border county.

sentences.zh: 御史文森、張津、曾大有言事下吏，崔誌端由道士擢尚書，天錫皆力爭。

translations.literal: When Censors Wen Sen, Zhang Jin, and Zeng Dayou spoke on affairs of state and were imprisoned, and when Cui Zhiduan was promoted from Daoist priest to minister, Tianxi contested each matter with all his force.
translations.idiomatic: When Censors Wen Sen, Zhang Jin, and Zeng Dayou spoke on affairs of state and were imprisoned, and when Cui Zhiduan was promoted from Daoist priest to minister, Tianxi contested each matter with all his force.

sentences.zh: 十七年五月，天變求言。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventeenth year, heaven-sent omens prompted a call for remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventeenth year, heaven-sent omens prompted a call for remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 上疏曰：「外官三年考察，又有撫按監臨，科道糾劾，其法已無可加。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "Provincial officials undergo triennial review, with further supervision by grand coordinators and surveillance commissioners and impeachment by the censorate and remonstrance bureaus; the system cannot be made stricter.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial saying: "Provincial officials undergo triennial review, with further supervision by grand coordinators and surveillance commissioners and impeachment by the censorate and remonstrance bureaus; the system cannot be made stricter.

sentences.zh: 惟兩京堂上官例不考核。

translations.literal: Only senior officials of the two capitals are by custom exempt from review.
translations.idiomatic: Only senior officials of the two capitals are by custom exempt from review.

sentences.zh: 而五品以下雖有十年考察之條，居官率限九載，或年勞轉遷，或服除改補，不能及期。

translations.literal: Yet although officials below the fifth rank have a rule of decennial review, most serve only nine years in a post, or transfer on merit, or return after mourning and receive a new appointment, and cannot reach the deadline.
translations.idiomatic: Yet although officials below the fifth rank have a rule of decennial review, most serve only nine years in a post, or transfer on merit, or return after mourning and receive a new appointment, and cannot reach the deadline.

sentences.zh: 今請以六年為期，通行考察。

translations.literal: I now ask that a six-year term be set and review be applied universally.
translations.idiomatic: I now ask that a six-year term be set and review be applied universally.

sentences.zh: 其大寮曾經彈劾者，悉令自陳而簡去之，用儆有位。

translations.literal: Those great ministers who have previously been impeached should all be ordered to submit self-accusations and be culled, to warn those in high office.
translations.idiomatic: Those great ministers who have previously been impeached should all be ordered to submit self-accusations and be culled, to warn those in high office.

sentences.zh: 古者，災異策免三公，陰霖輒避位。

translations.literal: In antiquity, calamities and portents led to the dismissal of the Three Dukes; prolonged rain would make them yield their posts.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, calamities and portents led to the dismissal of the Three Dukes; prolonged rain would make them yield their posts.

sentences.zh: 今大臣不引咎，陛下又不行策免，宜且革公孤銜，俟天心既回，徐還厥職。

translations.literal: Today the great ministers do not accept blame, and Your Majesty does not dismiss them; they should for the time being be stripped of their grand-counselor titles and wait until Heaven's mind turns again before slowly resuming their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Today the great ministers do not accept blame, and Your Majesty does not dismiss them; they should for the time being be stripped of their grand-counselor titles and wait until Heaven's mind turns again before slowly resuming their duties.

sentences.zh: 祖宗禦內官，恩不泛施，法不輕貸。

translations.literal: Our ancestors governed the inner eunuchs: favor was not spread indiscriminately, and the law was not lightly waived.
translations.idiomatic: Our ancestors governed the inner eunuchs: favor was not spread indiscriminately, and the law was not lightly waived.

sentences.zh: 內府二十四監局及在外管事者，並有常員。

translations.literal: The twenty-four directorates and offices of the inner palace, and those who manage affairs outside it, all had fixed quotas.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-four directorates and offices of the inner palace, and those who manage affairs outside it, all had fixed quotas.

sentences.zh: 近年諸監局掌印、僉事多至三四十人，他管事無數，留都亦然。

translations.literal: In recent years the seal-holders and vice-directors of the various directorates often number thirty or forty, and other managers are beyond count; the same is true at the secondary capital.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the seal-holders and vice-directors of the various directorates often number thirty or forty, and other managers are beyond count; the same is true at the secondary capital.

sentences.zh: 憑陵奢暴，蠹蝕民膏，第宅連雲，田園遍野，膏粱厭於輿臺，文繡被乎狗馬。

translations.literal: Overbearing and extravagant, they devour the people's substance; mansions touch the clouds and estates fill the countryside; fine grain cloys the mouths of carriage men, and brocade covers the backs of dogs and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Overbearing and extravagant, they devour the people's substance; mansions touch the clouds and estates fill the countryside; fine grain cloys the mouths of carriage men, and brocade covers the backs of dogs and horses.

sentences.zh: 凡若此類，皆足召變。

translations.literal: All such things are enough to summon calamity.
translations.idiomatic: All such things are enough to summon calamity.

sentences.zh: 乞敕司禮監會內閣嚴行考察，以定去留。

translations.literal: I beg that the Directorate of Ceremonial, together with the Grand Secretariat, be ordered to conduct strict review and fix who stays and who goes.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the Directorate of Ceremonial, together with the Grand Secretariat, be ordered to conduct strict review and fix who stays and who goes.

sentences.zh: 此後，或三年、五年一行，永為定制。」

translations.literal: Thereafter let review be carried out every three or five years as a permanent rule."
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter let review be carried out every three or five years as a permanent rule."

sentences.zh: 帝善之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 於是令兩京四品以上並自陳聽命，五品下六年考察，遂著為令。

translations.literal: Thereupon officials of the fourth rank and above in both capitals were ordered to submit self-accusations and await the throne's decision, and officials below the fifth rank were placed under six-year review; this was established as an ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon officials of the fourth rank and above in both capitals were ordered to submit self-accusations and await the throne's decision, and officials below the fifth rank were placed under six-year review; this was established as an ordinance.

sentences.zh: 惟大臣削公孤及內官考察，事格不行。

translations.literal: Only the stripping of grand-counselor titles from great ministers and review of the inner eunuchs was blocked and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Only the stripping of grand-counselor titles from great ministers and review of the inner eunuchs was blocked and not carried out.

sentences.zh: 尋與御史何深核牛馬房，條上便利十四事，歲省芻豆費五十余萬。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, together with Censor He Shen, he audited the Ox and Horse Stables and listed fourteen measures of benefit, saving more than five hundred thousand in fodder expenses each year.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, together with Censor He Shen, he audited the Ox and Horse Stables and listed fourteen measures of benefit, saving more than five hundred thousand in fodder expenses each year.

sentences.zh: 方瑾用事，橫甚，尤惡諫官，懼禍者往往自盡。

translations.literal: While Jin held power he was extremely overbearing and especially hated remonstrating officials; those who feared disaster often took their own lives.
translations.idiomatic: While Jin held power he was extremely overbearing and especially hated remonstrating officials; those who feared disaster often took their own lives.

sentences.zh: 海陽周鑰，弘治十五年進士。

translations.literal: Zhou Yao of Haiyang, a jinshi of the fifteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yao of Haiyang received his jinshi degree in the fifteenth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 為兵科給事中，勘事淮安，與知府趙俊善。

translations.literal: Serving as supervising secretary in the Office of War, he investigated affairs at Huai'an and became friendly with Prefect Zhao Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as supervising secretary in the Office of War, he investigated affairs at Huai'an and became friendly with Prefect Zhao Jun.

sentences.zh: 俊許貸千金，既而不與。

translations.literal: Jun promised to lend him a thousand taels of silver but afterward did not give it.
translations.idiomatic: Jun promised to lend him a thousand taels of silver but afterward did not give it.

sentences.zh: 時奉使還者，瑾皆索重賄。

translations.literal: At the time Jin demanded heavy bribes from all who returned from missions.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jin demanded heavy bribes from all who returned from missions.

sentences.zh: 鑰計無所出，舟行至桃源，自刎。

translations.literal: Yao could see no way out; when his boat reached Taoyuan he cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: Yao could see no way out; when his boat reached Taoyuan he cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 從者救之，已不能言，取紙書「趙知府誤我」，遂卒。

translations.literal: His attendants tried to save him, but he could no longer speak; he took paper and wrote "Prefect Zhao misled me," then died.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants tried to save him, but he could no longer speak; he took paper and wrote "Prefect Zhao misled me," then died.

sentences.zh: 事聞，系俊至京，責鑰死狀，竟坐俊罪。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Jun was brought to the capital in custody; Yao's death was laid at his door, and Jun was punished in the end.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported, Jun was brought to the capital in custody; Yao's death was laid at his door, and Jun was punished in the end.

sentences.zh: 平定郗夔，弘治十五年進士，為禮科給事中。

translations.literal: Xi Kui of Pingding, a jinshi of the fifteenth year of Hongzhi, served as supervising secretary in the Office of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Kui of Pingding received his jinshi degree in the fifteenth year of Hongzhi and served as supervising secretary in the Office of Rites.

sentences.zh: 正德五年，出核延綏戰功，瑾屬其私人。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengde he was sent out to verify military merit in Yan-Sui; Jin assigned the task to his own man.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhengde he was sent out to verify military merit in Yan-Sui; Jin assigned the task to his own man.

sentences.zh: 夔念從之則違國典，不從則得禍，遂自經死。

translations.literal: Kui thought that to obey would violate the national code, but to refuse would bring disaster; he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Kui thought that to obey would violate the national code, but to refuse would bring disaster; he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 瓊山馮颙，弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: Feng Yong of Qiongshan, a jinshi of the ninth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yong of Qiongshan received his jinshi degree in the ninth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 為御史，嘗以事忤瑾，為所誣，自經死。

translations.literal: Serving as censor, he once offended Jin on a matter and was framed by him; he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as censor, he once offended Jin on a matter and was framed by him; he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 颙初為主事，官軍討叛黎符南蛇久不克，颙歷陳致變之由，請購已革土官子孫，俾召集舊卒，以夷攻夷，有功則復舊職。

translations.literal: When Yong was still a director, government troops had long failed to subdue the rebel Li Fu Nan She; Yong set out in detail the causes of the uprising and asked that descendants of deposed native chiefs be recruited, so that they might gather old soldiers and use tribes against tribes, restoring their former posts if they achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong was still a director, government troops had long failed to subdue the rebel Li Fu Nan She; Yong set out in detail the causes of the uprising and asked that descendants of deposed native chiefs be recruited, so that they might gather old soldiers and use tribes against tribes, restoring their former posts if they achieved merit.

sentences.zh: 尚書劉大夏亟稱之，奏行其策。

translations.literal: Minister Liu Daxia praised him repeatedly and memorialized that his plan be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Liu Daxia praised him repeatedly and memorialized that his plan be adopted.

sentences.zh: 正德初，偕中官高金勘涇王所乞莊地，清還二千七百余頃。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde, together with the eunuch Gao Jin he investigated estate lands solicited by the Prince of Jing and cleared and returned more than twenty-seven hundred qing.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhengde, together with the eunuch Gao Jin he investigated estate lands solicited by the Prince of Jing and cleared and returned more than twenty-seven hundred qing.

sentences.zh: 而不得其死，人皆惜之。

translations.literal: Yet he did not meet a proper death, and all regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he did not meet a proper death, and all regretted it.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，天錫、鑰、夔、颙俱復官賜祭，且恤其家。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, Tianxi, Yao, Kui, and Yong all had their offices restored and were granted sacrificial rites, and their families were given relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was executed, Tianxi, Yao, Kui, and Yong all had their offices restored and were granted sacrificial rites, and their families were given relief.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，天錫子春訟冤，復賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign, Tianxi's son Chun petitioned over the injustice, and sacrificial burial was granted again.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiajing reign, Tianxi's son Chun petitioned over the injustice, and sacrificial burial was granted again.

sentences.zh: 方瑾敗時，刑部員外郎夾江宿進疏陳六事，言：「忤逆瑾死者，內臣如王嶽、範亨，言官如許天錫、周鑰，並宜恤贈。

translations.literal: Just as Jin was falling, Su Jin, an assistant department director of the Ministry of Justice from Jiajiang, submitted a memorial setting forth six matters, saying: "Those who died opposing Jin—inner attendants such as Wang Yue and Fan Heng, remonstrating officials such as Xu Tianxi and Zhou Yao—should all be given posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Jin was falling, Su Jin, an assistant department director of the Ministry of Justice from Jiajiang, submitted a memorial setting forth six matters, saying: "Those who died opposing Jin—inner attendants such as Wang Yue and Fan Heng, remonstrating officials such as Xu Tianxi and Zhou Yao—should all be given posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 又附瑾大臣，如兵部尚書王敞等及內侍余黨，俱宜斥。」

translations.literal: Again, great ministers who attached themselves to Jin, such as Minister of War Wang Chang and the like, and the remaining partisans among the inner attendants, should all be dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: Again, great ministers who attached themselves to Jin, such as Minister of War Wang Chang and the like, and the remaining partisans among the inner attendants, should all be dismissed."

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝怒將親鞫之，命張永召閣臣李東陽。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor grew angry and was about to interrogate him personally; he ordered Zhang Yong to summon Grand Secretary Li Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial entered, the emperor grew angry and was about to interrogate him personally; he ordered Zhang Yong to summon Grand Secretary Li Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 東陽語永曰：「後生狂妄，且日暮非見君時，幸少寬之。」

translations.literal: Dongyang said to Yong: "The young man is reckless, and with dusk falling this is no time to see the sovereign; please be a little lenient."
translations.idiomatic: Dongyang said to Yong: "The young man is reckless, and with dusk falling this is no time to see the sovereign; please be a little lenient."

sentences.zh: 永入，少頃執進至午門，杖五十，削籍歸，未幾卒。

translations.literal: Yong entered; shortly afterward Su Jin was seized and brought to the Meridian Gate, beaten fifty times, stripped of registry and sent home; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Yong entered; shortly afterward Su Jin was seized and brought to the Meridian Gate, beaten fifty times, stripped of registry and sent home; before long he died.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shizong reign he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrificial Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shizong reign he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrificial Office.

sentences.zh: 徐文溥，字可大，開化人。

translations.literal: Xu Wenpu, styled Keda, was a native of Kaihua.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wenpu, courtesy name Keda, came from Kaihua.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the sixth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixth year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 授南京禮科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Nanjing Office of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Nanjing Office of Rites.

sentences.zh: 劾尚書劉櫻、都御史李士實、侍郎呂獻、大理卿茆欽，而請召還致仕尚書孫交、傅珪。

translations.literal: He impeached Ministers Liu Ying and Li Shishi, Vice Minister Lu Xian, and Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Mao Qin, and asked that retired Ministers Sun Jiao and Fu Gui be recalled.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Ministers Liu Ying and Li Shishi, Vice Minister Lu Xian, and Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Mao Qin, and asked that retired Ministers Sun Jiao and Fu Gui be recalled.

sentences.zh: 時論以為當。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion held this appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion held this appropriate.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠求復護衛，文溥諫曰：「曩因寧藩不靖，英廟革其護衛、屯田。

translations.literal: When Prince Ning Chen Hao sought restoration of his bodyguard, Wenpu remonstrated, saying: "Formerly, because the Ning princely house was unsettled, Emperor Yingzong abolished its bodyguard and military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ning Chen Hao sought restoration of his bodyguard, Wenpu remonstrated, saying: "Formerly, because the Ning princely house was unsettled, Emperor Yingzong abolished its bodyguard and military colonies.

sentences.zh: 及逆瑾亂政，重賄謀復。

translations.literal: When the traitor Jin threw the government into chaos, heavy bribes were paid to plot restoration.
translations.idiomatic: When the traitor Jin threw the government into chaos, heavy bribes were paid to plot restoration.

sentences.zh: 瑾既伏誅，陛下又革之，正欲制以義而安全之耳。

translations.literal: After Jin had been executed, Your Majesty abolished it again, precisely to restrain him by righteousness and keep him safe.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin had been executed, Your Majesty abolished it again, precisely to restrain him by righteousness and keep him safe.

sentences.zh: 乃曰『驅使乏人』。

translations.literal: Yet now it is said, 'We lack men to drive and attend.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet now it is said, 'We lack men to drive and attend.'

sentences.zh: 夫晏居深邃，靡征討之勞，安享尊榮，無居守之責，何所用而乏人？

translations.literal: He dwells at ease in deep seclusion, without the toil of campaigns; he enjoys honor and glory, without the duty of guarding a post—what need has he of attendants?
translations.idiomatic: He dwells at ease in deep seclusion, without the toil of campaigns; he enjoys honor and glory, without the duty of guarding a post—what need has he of attendants?

sentences.zh: 且王暴行大彰：剝削商民，挾制官吏，招誘無賴，廣行劫掠。

translations.literal: Moreover the prince's violent conduct is widely known: he strips merchants, coerces officials, recruits ruffians, and carries out plunder on a broad scale.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the prince's violent conduct is widely known: he strips merchants, coerces officials, recruits ruffians, and carries out plunder on a broad scale.

sentences.zh: 致舟航斷絕，邑裏蕭條，萬民莫不切齒。

translations.literal: River traffic has been cut off and market towns lie desolate; ten thousand people gnash their teeth at him.
translations.idiomatic: River traffic has been cut off and market towns lie desolate; ten thousand people gnash their teeth at him.

sentences.zh: 乃今止之，猶恐不逮，顧可縱之加恣，假翼於虎乎？

translations.literal: Even to restrain him now may not be enough—how can he be allowed to grow more reckless and be given wings like a tiger?
translations.idiomatic: Even to restrain him now may not be enough—how can he be allowed to grow more reckless and be given wings like a tiger?

sentences.zh: 貢獻本有定制，乃無故馳騁飛騎，出入都城，伺察動靜。

translations.literal: Tribute missions follow fixed regulations, yet for no reason his swift riders gallop in and out of the capital, spying on movements.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute missions follow fixed regulations, yet for no reason his swift riders gallop in and out of the capital, spying on movements.

sentences.zh: 況今海內多故，天變未息，意外之虞實未易料。

translations.literal: Moreover, within the realm troubles are many, heaven-sent omens have not ceased, and unforeseen dangers are truly hard to foretell.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, within the realm troubles are many, heaven-sent omens have not ceased, and unforeseen dangers are truly hard to foretell.

sentences.zh: 宜裁以大義，勿徇私情，罪其獻謀之人，逐彼偵事之使，宗社幸甚。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should judge by great principle, not private feeling; punish those who offered the scheme and expel his spies—the altars of state would be greatly fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should judge by great principle, not private feeling; punish those who offered the scheme and expel his spies—the altars of state would be greatly fortunate."

sentences.zh: 時宸濠奧援甚眾，疏入，人鹹危之，帝但責其妄言而已。

translations.literal: At the time Chen Hao had many powerful backers; when the memorial entered, all feared for Wenpu, but the emperor only rebuked him for reckless speech.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Chen Hao had many powerful backers; when the memorial entered, all feared for Wenpu, but the emperor only rebuked him for reckless speech.

sentences.zh: 又請擇建儲貳，不報。

translations.literal: He also asked that an heir apparent be chosen and invested; there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that an heir apparent be chosen and invested; there was no reply.

sentences.zh: 十年四月復偕同官上疏曰：「頃因災異，禮部奏請修省。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the tenth year he again joined his colleagues in submitting a memorial, saying: "Recently, because of calamities and portents, the Ministry of Rites memorialized requesting self-reform.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the tenth year he again joined his colleagues in submitting a memorial, saying: "Recently, because of calamities and portents, the Ministry of Rites memorialized requesting self-reform.

sentences.zh: 伏讀聖諭，謂『事關朕躬者，皆已知之』。

translations.literal: Reading Your Majesty's edict in reverence, it says, 'Matters concerning my own person—I am already aware of them.'
translations.idiomatic: Reading Your Majesty's edict in reverence, it says, 'Matters concerning my own person—I am already aware of them.'

sentences.zh: 臣惟茲一念之誠，足以孚上帝迓休命矣。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that this single thought of sincerity is enough to win Heaven's trust and receive its blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject considers that this single thought of sincerity is enough to win Heaven's trust and receive its blessing.

sentences.zh: 雖然，知之非艱，行之維艱。

translations.literal: Yet though knowing is not hard, doing is hard.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though knowing is not hard, doing is hard.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能經筵講學，早朝勤政；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can truly attend lectures at the classics colloquium and hold early audiences with diligence;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty can truly attend lectures at the classics colloquium and hold early audiences with diligence;

sentences.zh: 布寬恤以安人心，躬獻享以重宗廟；

translations.literal: issue lenient edicts to reassure the people, and personally perform sacrificial offerings to honor the ancestral temples;
translations.idiomatic: proclaim clemency to settle the people's hearts, and go in person to the ancestral temples with offerings;

sentences.zh: 孝養慈闈，敬事蒼昊；

translations.literal: nourish the empress dowager in filial devotion, and reverently serve Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: nourish the empress dowager in filial devotion, and reverently serve Heaven;

sentences.zh: 舍豹房而居大內，遠嬖幸而近儒臣；

translations.literal: leave the Leopard Quarter and dwell in the inner palace, keep favored minions at a distance and draw Confucian ministers near;
translations.idiomatic: leave the Leopard Quarter and dwell in the inner palace, keep favored minions at a distance and draw Confucian ministers near;

sentences.zh: 禁中不為貿易，皇店不以罔財；

translations.literal: forbid trade within the palace, and stop the imperial shops from extorting wealth;
translations.idiomatic: forbid trade within the palace, and stop the imperial shops from extorting wealth;

sentences.zh: 還邊兵於故伍，斥番僧於外寺；

translations.literal: return frontier troops to their original units, and expel Tibetan monks from outside temples;
translations.idiomatic: return frontier troops to their original units, and expel Tibetan monks from outside temples;

sentences.zh: 毋昵俳優，盡屏義子；

translations.literal: do not dote on actors, and dismiss all adopted sons;
translations.idiomatic: do not dote on actors, and dismiss all adopted sons;

sentences.zh: 馬氏已醮之女弗留乎後宮，馬昂梟獍之族立奪其兵柄；

translations.literal: let not the already-married daughter of the Ma clan remain in the inner palace, and immediately strip the Ma Ang clan—worse than wolves and jackals—of its military command;
translations.idiomatic: let not the already-married daughter of the Ma clan remain in the inner palace, and immediately strip the Ma Ang clan—worse than wolves and jackals—of its military command;

sentences.zh: 停諸路之織造，罷不急之土木；

translations.literal: halt weaving commissions on every circuit, and stop non-urgent construction projects;
translations.idiomatic: halt weaving commissions on every circuit, and stop non-urgent construction projects;

sentences.zh: 汰倉局門戶之內官，禁水陸舟車之進奉；

translations.literal: cull the inner attendants at the granaries, bureaus, and gate offices, and forbid tribute sent by land and water, by cart and boat;
translations.idiomatic: cull the inner attendants at the granaries, bureaus, and gate offices, and forbid tribute sent by land and water, by cart and boat;

sentences.zh: 出留中奏牘以達下情，省傳奉冗員以慎名器。

translations.literal: release memorials held back at court so that grievances below may be heard, and reduce superfluous specially appointed posts to safeguard official titles.
translations.idiomatic: release memorials held back at court so that grievances below may be heard, and reduce superfluous specially appointed posts to safeguard official titles.

sentences.zh: 則陛下所謂『事關朕躬』，非徒知之，且一一行之，而不轉禍為福者，未之有也。」

translations.literal: Then what Your Majesty calls "matters concerning my own person" would not be merely known, but carried out one by one—and never has calamity failed to turn into blessing when that is done."
translations.idiomatic: Then what Your Majesty calls "matters concerning my own person" would be not only understood but truly enacted—and calamity would turn to blessing as never before."

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: The memorial was noted and filed.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was noted and filed.

sentences.zh: 初，帝聽中官崔瑤、史宣、劉瑯阝、於喜誣奏，先後逮知府翟唐，部曹王鑾、王瑞之，御史施儒、張經等，又入中官王堂譖，下僉事韓邦奇獄。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor had heeded false accusations by the inner attendants Cui Yao, Shi Xuan, Liu Lang, and Yu Xi, and in succession had arrested Prefect Zhai Tang, department secretaries Wang Luan and Wang Ruizhi, and Censors Shi Ru and Zhang Jing; he also accepted a slanderous report from the inner attendant Wang Tang and imprisoned Vice Commissioner Han Bangqi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the emperor had heeded false accusations by the inner attendants Cui Yao, Shi Xuan, Liu Lang, and Yu Xi, and in succession had arrested Prefect Zhai Tang, department secretaries Wang Luan and Wang Ruizhi, and Censors Shi Ru and Zhang Jing; he also accepted a slanderous report from the inner attendant Wang Tang and imprisoned Vice Commissioner Han Bangqi.

sentences.zh: 文溥言：「朝廷刑威所及，乃在奄侍一言。

translations.literal: Wenpu said: "The reach of the court's penal authority now depends on a single word from a eunuch attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Wenpu said: "The court's penal reach now hangs on a single word from a palace eunuch.

sentences.zh: 旗校繹絡於道途，縉紳駢首於狴犴，遠近震駭，上下屏氣。

translations.literal: Brocade guards swarm along the roads; gentry and officials are herded into prison; near and far are shaken with terror, and above and below hold their breath.
translations.idiomatic: Brocade guards swarm along the roads; gentry and officials are herded into prison; near and far are shaken with terror, and above and below hold their breath.

sentences.zh: 向一瑾亂政於內，今數瑾縱橫於外。

translations.literal: Once there was one Jin who threw the government into chaos within; now there are many Jins who run rampant without.
translations.idiomatic: Once one Jin threw the government into chaos from within; now a host of Jins run rampant without.

sentences.zh: 乞並下堂法司，且追治瑤等誣罔罪。」

translations.literal: I beg that Tang be handed over to the regular judiciary, and that Yao and the others be prosecuted for false accusation."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Tang be handed over to the regular judiciary, and that Yao and the others be prosecuted for false accusation."

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，遂引疾去。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen, and Wenpu thereupon resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen, and Wenpu thereupon resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，廷臣交薦，起河南參議。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, court officials jointly recommended him, and he was recalled as administration commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, court officials jointly recommended him, and he was recalled as administration commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以念母乞歸。

translations.literal: Before long, longing for his mother, he begged to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, longing for his mother, he begged to return home.

sentences.zh: 撫按請移近地便養，乃改福建。

translations.literal: The grand coordinator and surveillance commissioner asked that he be moved nearer so he could more easily support his mother, and he was therefore transferred to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: The grand coordinator and surveillance commissioner asked that he be moved nearer so he could more easily support his mother, and he was therefore transferred to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 尋遷廣東副使。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to vice commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to vice commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 上言十事，多涉權要，恐貽母憂，復引疾歸。

translations.literal: He submitted ten proposals, many touching powerful figures; fearing this would bring grief to his mother, he again resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted ten proposals, many touching powerful figures; fearing this would bring grief to his mother, he again resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 行至玉山卒。

translations.literal: He died at Yushan while on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Yushan while on the road.

sentences.zh: 翟唐，字堯佐，長垣人。

translations.literal: Zhai Tang, styled Yaozuo, was a native of Changyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Tang, courtesy name Yaozuo, came from Changyuan.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twelfth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twelfth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 由壽光知縣召為御史。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Shouguang he was summoned to serve as censor.
translations.idiomatic: From magistrate of Shouguang he was summoned to serve as censor.

sentences.zh: 正德四年出按湖廣，奏言：「四川賊首劉烈僭號設官，必將為大患。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengde he was sent out to inspect Huguang and memorialized: "The bandit chieftain Liu Lie in Sichuan has assumed a title and established offices; he is certain to become a great scourge.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhengde he was sent out to inspect Huguang and memorialized: "The bandit chieftain Liu Lie in Sichuan has assumed a title and established offices; he is certain to become a great scourge.

sentences.zh: 湖廣、陜西壤地相接，入竹山可抵荊、襄，入漢中可抵秦、隴。

translations.literal: Huguang and Shaanxi share a border; by entering Zhushan one can reach Jing and Xiang, and by entering Hanzhong one can reach Qin and Long.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang and Shaanxi share a border; by entering Zhushan one can reach Jing and Xiang, and by entering Hanzhong one can reach Qin and Long.

sentences.zh: 今內外壅蔽，獎諭切責率皆虛文，宜切圖預備之策。」

translations.literal: Now obstruction blocks both within and without, and rewards, admonitions, and stern rebukes are all empty form; urgent plans of defense should be drawn up.
translations.idiomatic: Now obstruction blocks both within and without, and rewards, admonitions, and stern rebukes are all empty form; urgent plans of defense should be drawn up.

sentences.zh: 時劉瑾竊柄，以唐言「壅蔽」，尤惡之。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Jin held power in secret, and because Tang's words spoke of "obstruction," he especially hated him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liu Jin held power in secret, and because Tang's words spoke of "obstruction," he especially hated him.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書王敞希指，言今蕩滌宿弊，唐乃雲然，宜令指實。

translations.literal: Minister of War Wang Chang, seeking to please Jin, said that now accumulated abuses were being swept away, yet Tang spoke as he did; Tang should be ordered to substantiate his charges.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Wang Chang, seeking to please Jin, said that now accumulated abuses were being swept away, yet Tang spoke as he did; Tang should be ordered to substantiate his charges.

sentences.zh: 會瑾怒稍解，乃切責而宥之。

translations.literal: When Jin's anger had eased somewhat, Tang was sternly rebuked but spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin's anger had eased somewhat, Tang was sternly rebuked but spared.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷知寧波府。

translations.literal: After some time he was transferred to prefect of Ningbo.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was transferred to prefect of Ningbo.

sentences.zh: 市舶中官崔瑤藉貢物擾民，為唐所裁抑，且杖其黨王臣，臣尋病死。

translations.literal: The maritime-trade eunuch Cui Yao used tribute goods to harass the people and was restrained by Tang, who also had his follower Wang Chen beaten; Chen soon died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The maritime-trade eunuch Cui Yao used tribute goods to harass the people and was restrained by Tang, who also had his follower Wang Chen beaten; Chen soon died of illness.

sentences.zh: 瑤奏唐阻截貢獻，笞殺貢使。

translations.literal: Yao memorialized that Tang had obstructed tribute missions and beaten a tribute envoy to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yao memorialized that Tang had obstructed tribute missions and beaten a tribute envoy to death.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，逮下詔獄。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry and had Tang arrested and imprisoned in the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry and had Tang arrested and imprisoned in the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史趙春等交章救之。

translations.literal: Surveillance Commissioner Zhao Chun and others submitted successive memorials in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance Commissioner Zhao Chun and others submitted successive memorials in his defense.

sentences.zh: 給事中範洵亦言唐被逮日，軍民遮道涕泣，請宥令還任。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Fan Xun also said that on the day Tang was arrested, soldiers and civilians blocked the road in tears and begged that he be pardoned and returned to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Fan Xun also said that on the day Tang was arrested, soldiers and civilians blocked the road in tears and begged that he be pardoned and returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，謫雲南嵩明知州。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen and demoted Tang to magistrate of Songming in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen and demoted Tang to magistrate of Songming in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 再遷陜西副使卒。

translations.literal: After a further promotion to vice commissioner of Shaanxi, he died.
translations.idiomatic: After a further promotion to vice commissioner of Shaanxi, he died.

sentences.zh: 王鑾，字廷和，大庾人。

translations.literal: Wang Luan, styled Tinghe, was a native of Dayu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Luan, courtesy name Tinghe, came from Dayu.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the third year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 授邵武知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Shaowu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Shaowu.

sentences.zh: 入為都水主事，出轄徐沛閘河。

translations.literal: He entered service as a director in the Directorate of Waterways and was sent out to oversee the sluice-works of Xu and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a director in the Directorate of Waterways and was sent out to oversee the sluice-works of Xu and Pei.

sentences.zh: 十一年，織造中官史宣過其地，索挽夫千人，沛縣知縣胡守約給其半。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, the weaving eunuch Shi Xuan passed through the region and demanded a thousand boat haulers; Magistrate Hu Shouyue of Pei County supplied half that number.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, the weaving eunuch Shi Xuan passed through the region and demanded a thousand boat haulers; Magistrate Hu Shouyue of Pei County supplied half that number.

sentences.zh: 宣怒，自至縣捕吏，鑾助守約與抗。

translations.literal: Xuan grew angry, came in person to the county to seize clerks, and Luan aided Shouyue in resisting him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan grew angry, came in person to the county to seize clerks, and Luan aided Shouyue in resisting him.

sentences.zh: 宣誣奏於朝，逮系詔獄。

translations.literal: Xuan lodged a false accusation at court, and Luan was arrested and imprisoned in the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan lodged a false accusation at court, and Luan was arrested and imprisoned in the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 以言官論救，守約罷官，鑾輸贖還職。

translations.literal: Thanks to remonstrating officials pleading for him, Shouyue was dismissed from office and Luan paid a fine to ransom himself and return to duty.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to remonstrating officials pleading for him, Shouyue was dismissed from office and Luan paid a fine to ransom himself and return to duty.

sentences.zh: 已，分司南旺，又捕誅中官廖堂侄廖鵬之黨。

translations.literal: Later, while serving at Nanwang, he again captured and executed followers of Liao Peng, nephew of the eunuch Liao Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while serving at Nanwang, he again captured and executed followers of Liao Peng, nephew of the eunuch Liao Tang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，遷武昌知府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jiajing reign he was promoted to prefect of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jiajing reign he was promoted to prefect of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 鎮守中官李景儒歲進魚鲊多科率，鑾疏請罷之。

translations.literal: The garrison eunuch Li Jingru each year submitted pickled fish and imposed heavy levies; Luan memorialized asking that the practice be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison eunuch Li Jingru each year submitted pickled fish and imposed heavy levies; Luan memorialized asking that the practice be abolished.

sentences.zh: 楚府征稅，茶商重困。

translations.literal: The Prince of Chu's tax levies had left tea merchants in deep distress.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Chu's tax levies had left tea merchants in deep distress.

sentences.zh: 鑾謂稅當歸官，力與爭，王詆為毀辱親王。

translations.literal: Luan held that the taxes should belong to the government and contested the matter forcefully; the prince denounced him for insulting a royal kinsman.
translations.idiomatic: Luan held that the taxes should belong to the government and contested the matter forcefully; the prince denounced him for insulting a royal kinsman.

sentences.zh: 鑾遂請終養，不待報竟歸。

translations.literal: Luan thereupon asked to retire and support his parents, and without waiting for a reply went home.
translations.idiomatic: Luan thereupon asked to retire and support his parents, and without waiting for a reply went home.

sentences.zh: 後吏部坐以擅離職守，奪官。

translations.literal: Later the Ministry of Personnel punished him for leaving his post without authorization and stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Ministry of Personnel punished him for leaving his post without authorization and stripped him of office.

sentences.zh: 張士隆，字仲修，安陽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shilong, styled Zhongxiu, was a native of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shilong, courtesy name Zhongxiu, came from Anyang.

sentences.zh: 弘治八年舉鄉試，入太學。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Hongzhi he passed the provincial examination and entered the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Hongzhi he passed the provincial examination and entered the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 與同縣崔銑及寇天敘、馬卿、呂柟輩相砥礪，以學行聞。

translations.literal: Together with his townsman Cui Xuan and Kou Tianxu, Ma Qing, Lu Shan, and others, he sharpened one another in learning and conduct and became known for both.
translations.idiomatic: Together with his townsman Cui Xuan and Kou Tianxu, Ma Qing, Lu Shan, and others, he sharpened one another in learning and conduct and became known for both.

sentences.zh: 十八年成進士，授廣信推官。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he became a jinshi and was appointed investigating magistrate of Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he became a jinshi and was appointed investigating magistrate of Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 正德六年入為御史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengde he entered service as a censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhengde he entered service as a censor.

sentences.zh: 巡鹽河東，劾去貪汙運使劉愉。

translations.literal: While inspecting the salt administration of Hedong, he impeached and removed the corrupt transport commissioner Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting the salt administration of Hedong, he impeached and removed the corrupt transport commissioner Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 建正學書院，興起文教。

translations.literal: He founded the Zhengxue Academy and revived literary and moral instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the Zhengxue Academy and revived literary and moral instruction.

sentences.zh: 九年，乾清宮災，上疏曰：「陛下前有逆瑾之變，後遭薊盜之亂，猶不知警。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when the Qianqing Palace burned, he submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty has already suffered the upheaval of the traitor Jin and afterward the disorder of bandits in Ji—yet still you do not take warning.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when the Qianqing Palace burned, he submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty has already suffered the upheaval of the traitor Jin and afterward the disorder of bandits in Ji—yet still you do not take warning.

sentences.zh: 方且興居無度，狎昵匪人。

translations.literal: You still live without measure and draw close to unworthy men.
translations.idiomatic: You still live without measure and draw close to unworthy men.

sentences.zh: 積戎醜於禁中，戲幹戈於臥內。

translations.literal: You hoard weapons within the forbidden precinct and sport with arms in your bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: You stockpile arms in the inner palace and play with weapons beside your bed.

sentences.zh: 徹旦燕遊，萬幾不理。

translations.literal: You feast and roam until dawn, and leave the myriad affairs of state untended.
translations.idiomatic: You feast and roam until dawn, and leave the myriad affairs of state untended.

sentences.zh: 寵信內侍，濁亂朝綱。

translations.literal: You trust inner attendants and foul the order of the court.
translations.idiomatic: You trust inner attendants and foul the order of the court.

sentences.zh: 致民困盜起，財盡兵疲。

translations.literal: The people are distressed and bandits have risen; wealth is exhausted and troops worn out.
translations.idiomatic: The people are distressed and bandits have risen; wealth is exhausted and troops worn out.

sentences.zh: 禍機潛蓄，恐大命難保。

translations.literal: Disaster smolders beneath the surface; I fear the Mandate may not long endure.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster smolders beneath the surface; I fear the Mandate may not long endure.

sentences.zh: 夫裒衣博帶之雅，孰與市井狡儈之群？

translations.literal: What is the elegance of broad robes and sashes compared with the company of market sharpers?
translations.idiomatic: Is the dignity of scholar's dress worth less than the company of market rogues?

sentences.zh: 廣廈細旃之娛，孰與鞍馬驅馳之險？」

translations.literal: What is the pleasure of broad halls and fine mats compared with the peril of saddle and spur?"
translations.idiomatic: What is the pleasure of broad halls and fine mats compared with the peril of saddle and spur?"

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: There was no reply.

sentences.zh: 出按鳳陽。

translations.literal: He was sent out to inspect Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to inspect Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 織造中官史宣列黃梃二於騶前，號為「賜棍」，每以抶人，有至死者，自都御史以下莫敢問，士隆劾奏之。
