translations.literal: The weaving eunuch Shi Xuan placed two yellow clubs before his outriders and called them "gifted cudgels"; he used them to beat people, and some died; from the censor-in-chief downward none dared question him, and Shilong impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: The weaving eunuch Shi Xuan set two yellow clubs before his escort and called them "Imperial gifts"; he used them to beat men, and some died. From the censor-in-chief down, none dared intervene—until Shilong impeached him.

sentences.zh: 又劾錦衣千戶廖鎧奸利事，且曰：「鎧虐陜西，即其父鵬虐河南故習也。

translations.literal: He also impeached the brocade-guard commander Liao Kai for corrupt profit, saying: "Kai abused Shaanxi just as his father Peng abused Henan by old habit.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached the brocade-guard commander Liao Kai for corrupt profit, saying: "Kai abused Shaanxi just as his father Peng abused Henan by old habit.

sentences.zh: 河南以鵬故召亂，鎧又欲亂陜西。

translations.literal: Henan was thrown into disorder because of Peng; Kai now seeks to throw Shaanxi into disorder as well.
translations.idiomatic: Henan was thrown into disorder because of Peng; Kai now seeks to throw Shaanxi into disorder as well.

sentences.zh: 乞置鎧父子於法，並召還廖鑾，以釋陜人之憤。」

translations.literal: I beg that father and son Kai be punished by law, and that Liao Luan be recalled, to appease the anger of the people of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that father and son Kai be punished by law, and that Liao Luan be recalled, to appease the anger of the people of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 鑾，鎧所從鎮陜西者也。

translations.literal: Luan was the man from whom Kai had set out to garrison Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Luan was the man from whom Kai had set out to garrison Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 錢寧素昵鎧，見疏大恨，遂因士隆按薛鳳鳴獄以陷之。

translations.literal: Qian Ning was on intimate terms with Kai; when he saw the memorial he was deeply enraged, and therefore used Shilong's investigation of the Xue Fengming case to trap him.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Ning was on intimate terms with Kai; when he saw the memorial he was deeply enraged, and therefore used Shilong's investigation of the Xue Fengming case to trap him.

sentences.zh: 鳳鳴者，寶坻人，先為御史，坐罪削籍，諂事諸佞幸，尤善寧。

translations.literal: Fengming was a native of Baodi; he had earlier served as censor, was convicted and struck from the rolls, and fawned upon various favored sycophants, especially cultivating Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Fengming was a native of Baodi; he had earlier served as censor, was convicted and struck from the rolls, and fawned upon various favored sycophants, especially cultivating Ning.

sentences.zh: 與從弟鳳翔有隙，嗾緝事者發其私，下吏論死。

translations.literal: He had a feud with his cousin Fengxiang and instigated investigators to expose Fengxiang's private affairs; Fengxiang was imprisoned and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: He had a feud with his cousin Fengxiang and instigated investigators to expose Fengxiang's private affairs; Fengxiang was imprisoned and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 刑部疑有冤，並捕鞫鳳鳴。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice suspected there had been a miscarriage of justice and arrested and tried Fengming as well.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice suspected there had been a miscarriage of justice and arrested and tried Fengming as well.

sentences.zh: 鳳鳴懼，使其妾訴枉，自剄長安門外，詞連寶坻知縣周在及素所仇者數十人，悉逮付法司，而鳳鳴得釋。

translations.literal: Fengming, in fear, had his concubine plead injustice; she cut her throat outside Chang'an Gate, and the accusation implicated Magistrate Zhou Zai of Baodi and several dozen others whom Fengming had long hated—all were arrested and handed to the judiciary, while Fengming was released.
translations.idiomatic: Fengming, in fear, had his concubine plead injustice; she cut her throat outside Chang'an Gate, and the accusation implicated Magistrate Zhou Zai of Baodi and several dozen others whom Fengming had long hated—all were arrested and handed to the judiciary, while Fengming was released.

sentences.zh: 士隆與御史許完先後按治，復捕鳳鳴對簿，釋在還職。

translations.literal: Shilong and Censor Xu Wan successively investigated the case, rearrested Fengming for trial, and released Zai and restored him to office.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong and Censor Xu Wan successively investigated the case, rearrested Fengming for trial, and released Zai and restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 寧怒，令鳳鳴女告士隆、完治獄偏枉。

translations.literal: Ning grew angry and had Fengming's daughter accuse Shilong and Wan of partiality in handling the case.
translations.idiomatic: Ning grew angry and had Fengming's daughter accuse Shilong and Wan of partiality in handling the case.

sentences.zh: 遂下詔獄，謫士隆晉州判官。

translations.literal: Shilong was thereupon imprisoned in the imperial prison and demoted to assistant magistrate of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong was thereupon imprisoned in the imperial prison and demoted to assistant magistrate of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢知州。

translations.literal: After some time he was promoted to magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was promoted to magistrate.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，詔復故官，出為陜西副使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, an edict restored him to his former rank, and he was sent out as vice commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, an edict restored him to his former rank, and he was sent out as vice commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 漢中賊王大等匿豪家，結回回為亂。

translations.literal: In Hanzhong the bandit Wang Da and others hid among powerful families and joined with Hui Muslims to raise rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In Hanzhong the bandit Wang Da and others hid among powerful families and joined with Hui Muslims to raise rebellion.

sentences.zh: 士隆下令：匿賊者罪及妻孥，無赦。

translations.literal: Shilong issued an order: whoever harbored bandits would have guilt extended to wife and children, without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong issued an order: whoever harbored bandits would have guilt extended to wife and children, without pardon.

sentences.zh: 賊無所容，遂就擒滅。

translations.literal: With nowhere to hide, the bandits were captured and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: With nowhere to hide, the bandits were captured and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 築堰溉田千頃，民利之。

translations.literal: He built dikes and irrigated a thousand qing of fields, to the people's benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He built dikes and irrigated a thousand qing of fields, to the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 張文明，字應奎，陽曲人。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenming, styled Yingkui, was a native of Yangqu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenming, courtesy name Yingkui, came from Yangqu.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the sixth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixth year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 授行人，擢御史，巡按遼東。

translations.literal: He was appointed a courier, then promoted to censor and sent to inspect Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a courier, then promoted to censor and sent to inspect Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 尋按陜西。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he inspected Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he inspected Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 鎮守中官廖堂貪恣，文明捕治其爪牙二十四人，堂大恨。

translations.literal: The garrison eunuch Liao Tang was greedy and unrestrained; Wenming arrested and punished twenty-four of his agents, and Tang deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison eunuch Liao Tang was greedy and unrestrained; Wenming arrested and punished twenty-four of his agents, and Tang deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 十三年，車駕幸延綏。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the imperial carriage visited Yan-Sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the imperial carriage visited Yan-Sui.

sentences.zh: 文明馳疏諫，極陳災異，且言江彬逢惡導非，亟宜行誅。

translations.literal: Wenming sent an urgent memorial remonstrating, setting forth omens and calamities at length, and saying that Jiang Bin met evil and led the emperor astray—that he should be executed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Wenming sent an urgent memorial of remonstrance, laying out heaven's warnings at length and declaring that Jiang Bin had embraced wickedness and led the emperor astray—that he ought to be put to death without delay.

sentences.zh: 朝臣匡救無聞，亦當罰治。

translations.literal: That court ministers had been heard offering no rescue should also be punished.
translations.idiomatic: The court ministers who had failed to intervene should likewise be punished.

sentences.zh: 帝不省。

translations.literal: The emperor took no heed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 既而文明朝行在。

translations.literal: Before long Wenming attended court at the imperial encampment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wenming presented himself at the emperor's traveling court.

sentences.zh: 諸權幸扈從者，文明裁抑之，所需多不應。

translations.literal: The favored minions in the imperial retinue Wenming restrained; many of their demands he refused.
translations.idiomatic: He checked the powerful favorites in the imperial retinue and refused most of what they demanded.

sentences.zh: 司禮太監張忠等譖於帝，言諸生毆旗校，文明縱勿治。

translations.literal: The director of ceremonial Zhang Zhong and others slandered him to the emperor, saying that students had beaten brocade guards and Wenming had let the matter go unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: The director of ceremonial Zhang Zhong and others denounced him to the emperor, claiming that students had beaten brocade guards and that Wenming had let them go unpunished.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命械赴京師，下詔獄。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry, ordered him shackled and sent to the capital, and imprisoned him in the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, had him shackled and sent to the capital, and cast him into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 明年春，言官交章請宥，不報。

translations.literal: The next spring, remonstrating officials submitted successive memorials asking pardon; there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring, remonstrating officials submitted memorial after memorial pleading for mercy—but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 比駕旋，命執至豹房，帝將親鞫。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, he was ordered brought to the Leopard Quarter; the emperor intended to interrogate him personally.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession returned, Wenming was brought to the Leopard Quarter, where the emperor meant to question him in person.

sentences.zh: 文明自謂必死。

translations.literal: Wenming believed he would surely die.
translations.idiomatic: Wenming was certain he would die.

sentences.zh: 及見帝，命釋之，謫電白典史。

translations.literal: When he saw the emperor, he was ordered released and demoted to recorder of Dianbai.
translations.idiomatic: When he at last faced the emperor, he was released—but demoted to recorder of Dianbai.

sentences.zh: 時劉瑾雖誅，佞幸猶熾，中外諫官被禍者不可勝數。

translations.literal: Though Liu Jin had been executed, favored sycophants still flourished; remonstrating officials within and without who suffered disaster were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Though Liu Jin was dead, favored sycophants still held sway, and remonstrating officials inside and outside the court who met ruin were beyond number.

sentences.zh: 文明止於貶謫，人以為幸。

translations.literal: Wenming suffered only demotion and exile; people considered him fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Wenming escaped with nothing worse than demotion and exile—many counted him lucky.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，召復故官，尋出為松江知府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, Wenming was recalled to his former rank and soon sent out as prefect of Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, Wenming was restored to his former rank and soon appointed prefect of Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 甫抵任，卒。

translations.literal: He had barely reached his post when he died.
translations.idiomatic: He had scarcely taken up his post when he died.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史馬錄頌其忠，詔贈太常少卿。

translations.literal: Surveillance Commissioner Ma Lu praised his loyalty, and an edict posthumously made him Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance Commissioner Ma Lu commended his loyalty, and the throne posthumously made him Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 陳鼎，字大器，其先宣城人。

translations.literal: Chen Ding, styled Daqi, was descended from men of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ding, courtesy name Daqi, came from a family originally of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 高祖尚書迪，死惠帝之難，子孫戍登州衛，遂占籍焉。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather, Minister Di, died in the troubles of Emperor Hui; his descendants were garrisoned at Dengzhou Guard and there took up registry.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather, the minister Di, perished in the troubles of Emperor Hui; the family was assigned to Dengzhou Guard and registered there.

sentences.zh: 鼎舉弘治十八年進士。

translations.literal: Ding passed the jinshi examination in the eighteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Ding received his jinshi degree in the eighteenth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 正德四年授禮科試給事中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengde he was appointed probationary supervising secretary in the Office of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhengde he was appointed probationary supervising secretary in the Office of Rites.

sentences.zh: 鎮守河南中官廖堂，福建人也，弟鵬之子鎧冒籍中河南鄉試。

translations.literal: The garrison eunuch Liao Tang of Henan, a native of Fujian, had his brother Peng's son Kai falsely register and pass the Henan provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan garrison eunuch Liao Tang, a Fujian native, had his brother Peng's son Kai fraudulently register and pass the Henan provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 物議沸騰，畏堂莫敢與難。

translations.literal: Public opinion seethed, but fearing Tang none dared raise objection.
translations.idiomatic: Public outrage ran high, yet fear of Tang kept anyone from challenging the matter.

sentences.zh: 鼎上章發其事，鎧遂除名，堂、鵬大恨。

translations.literal: Ding submitted a memorial exposing the affair; Kai was struck from the rolls, and Tang and Peng deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Ding memorialized and exposed the affair; Kai was struck from the rolls, and Tang and Peng came to hate him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 會流寇起，鼎陳弭盜機宜。

translations.literal: When roving bandits rose, Ding set forth measures to quell the brigands.
translations.idiomatic: When roving bandits rose up, Ding laid out measures for suppressing them.

sentences.zh: 堂囑權幸摘其語激帝怒，下詔獄掠治。

translations.literal: Tang had favored minions pluck phrases from his words to inflame the emperor's anger; Ding was imprisoned in the imperial prison and tortured.
translations.idiomatic: Tang had his powerful allies cherry-pick phrases from Ding's words to enrage the emperor; Ding was thrown into the imperial prison and tortured.

sentences.zh: 謂鼎前籍平江伯資產，附劉瑾增估物價，疑有侵盜。

translations.literal: It was charged that Ding had earlier inventoried the Duke of Pingjiang's assets, attached himself to Liu Jin to inflate valuations, and was suspected of embezzlement.
translations.idiomatic: He was accused of having earlier inventoried the Duke of Pingjiang's estate, colluded with Liu Jin to inflate valuations, and embezzled the difference.

sentences.zh: 尚書楊一清救之，乃釋為民。

translations.literal: Minister Yang Yiqing rescued him, and he was released as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Yang Yiqing intervened on his behalf, and he was released to live as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，復故官，遷河南參議。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, Ding was restored to his former rank and transferred to administration commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong took the throne, Ding was restored to office and made administration commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 妖人馬隆等為亂，鼎督兵誅之。

translations.literal: The sorcerer Ma Long and others raised rebellion; Ding led troops and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: The sorcerer Ma Long and his followers rose in rebellion; Ding led troops and put them down.

sentences.zh: 改陜西副使，擢浙江按察使，廉介正直，不通私謁。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner of Shaanxi, then promoted to surveillance commissioner of Zhejiang—incorruptible, upright, and accepting no private audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to vice commissioner of Shaanxi and then promoted to surveillance commissioner of Zhejiang, he was incorruptible and upright and would accept no private audiences.

sentences.zh: 召為應天府尹，未任卒。

translations.literal: He was summoned to be prefect of Yingtian but died before taking office.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as prefect of Yingtian but died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 賀泰，字誌同，吳縣人。

translations.literal: He Tai, styled Zhitong, was a native of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: He Tai, courtesy name Zhitong, came from Wu County.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twelfth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twelfth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 由衢州府推官入為御史。

translations.literal: From investigating magistrate of Quzhou Prefecture he entered service as censor.
translations.idiomatic: From investigating magistrate of Quzhou Prefecture he was appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 武宗收京師無賴及宦官廝養為義子，一日而賜國姓者百二十七人，泰抗言其非。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong took Beijing riffraff and eunuchs' fosterlings as adopted sons; in a single day one hundred twenty-seven were granted the imperial surname, and Tai remonstrated that this was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong took Beijing riffraff and eunuchs' fosterlings as adopted sons; in one day he granted the imperial surname to one hundred twenty-seven men, and Tai protested that this was wrong.

sentences.zh: 諸人激帝怒，謫衢州推官，終廣東參議。

translations.literal: Those men incited the emperor's anger; Tai was demoted to investigating magistrate of Quzhou and ended as administration commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: His enemies enraged the emperor; Tai was demoted to investigating magistrate of Quzhou and ended his career as administration commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 張璞，字中善，江夏人。

translations.literal: Zhang Pu, styled Zhongshan, was a native of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pu, courtesy name Zhongshan, came from Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 弘治十八年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the eighteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the eighteenth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 由歸安知縣召授御史。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Gui'an he was summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: From magistrate of Gui'an he was summoned to serve as censor.

sentences.zh: 正德八年出按雲南。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhengde he was sent out to inspect Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhengde he was sent to inspect Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 鎮守中官梁裕貪橫，璞裁抑之。

translations.literal: The garrison eunuch Liang Yu was greedy and overbearing; Pu restrained him.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison eunuch Liang Yu was greedy and overbearing; Pu checked his excesses.

sentences.zh: 為所誣，逮赴詔獄，死獄中。

translations.literal: Framed by Yu, he was arrested and sent to the imperial prison, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: Framed by Yu, he was seized and sent to the imperial prison, where he died.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，贈太仆少卿，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded to the throne, Pu was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and granted sacrificial burial.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong succeeded to the throne, Pu was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and granted state funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 成文，大同山陰人。

translations.literal: Cheng Wen was a native of Shanyin in Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Wen came from Shanyin in Datong.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the fifteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifteenth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 由知縣擢御史。

translations.literal: From magistrate he was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: From magistrate he was promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 正德中，阿爾禿廝、亦不剌與小王子戰敗，引所部駐甘肅塞外，時入寇，掠陷堡寨五十有三。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde reign, Altanishi, Yibulai, and the Small Prince were defeated in battle; they led their followers to camp beyond the Gansu frontier and from time to time raided inward, plundering and capturing fifty-three fortified posts.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign, Altanishi, Yibulai, and the Small Prince were defeated in battle and withdrew with their followers to camp beyond the Gansu frontier, raiding inward from time to time and overrunning fifty-three fortified posts.

sentences.zh: 巡撫張翼、鎮守太監朱彬等反冒奏首功千九百有余，以捷奏者十有一。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Zhang Yi, garrison director Zhu Bin, and others falsely reported more than nineteen hundred enemy heads; eleven victory memorials were submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zhang Yi, garrison director Zhu Bin, and others falsely claimed more than nineteen hundred enemy heads and submitted eleven victory memorials.

sentences.zh: 文出巡按，盡發其奸。

translations.literal: Wen went out on inspection and fully exposed their fraud.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen went out on inspection, he exposed their fraud in full.

sentences.zh: 翼等賄中人傾文。

translations.literal: Yi and the others bribed inner attendants to bring Wen down.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and his allies bribed palace eunuchs to bring Wen down.

sentences.zh: 會文劾僉事趙應龍，應龍亦訐文細事，遂逮文，斥為民。

translations.literal: When Wen impeached Vice Commissioner Zhao Yinglong, Yinglong in turn denounced Wen over petty matters; Wen was arrested and reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen impeached Vice Commissioner Zhao Yinglong, Yinglong retaliated with petty accusations; Wen was arrested and stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中起用，累官右副都御史巡撫遼東，告歸，卒。

translations.literal: Recalled in the Jiajing reign, he rose to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Liaodong, then requested retirement and died.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled during the Jiajing reign, he rose to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Liaodong, retired on his own request, and died.

sentences.zh: 李翰臣，大同人。

translations.literal: Li Hanchen was a native of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hanchen came from Datong.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the third year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 官御史，巡按山東。

translations.literal: He served as censor and was sent to inspect Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as censor and was sent to inspect Shandong.

sentences.zh: 吏部主事梁谷誣歸善王當沍謀叛，翰臣劾谷挾私。

translations.literal: Department director Liang Gu falsely accused Prince Guishan Danghu of plotting rebellion; Hanchen impeached Gu for private malice.
translations.idiomatic: Department director Liang Gu falsely accused Prince Guishan Danghu of plotting rebellion; Hanchen impeached Gu for acting out of private malice.

sentences.zh: 近幸方欲邀功，責翰臣為叛人掩飾。

translations.literal: Favored minions were then seeking credit and charged that Hanchen was covering for a rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial favorites seeking credit accused Hanchen of shielding a rebel.

sentences.zh: 逮系詔獄，謫德州判官。

translations.literal: He was arrested and imprisoned in the imperial prison, then demoted to assistant magistrate of Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was arrested and thrown into the imperial prison, then demoted to assistant magistrate of Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 終山東副使。

translations.literal: He ended as vice commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as vice commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 張經，興州左衛人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jing was a native of Xingzhou Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jing came from Xingzhou Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the sixth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixth year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 官御史。

translations.literal: He served as censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as censor.

sentences.zh: 出按宣府，劾鎮守中官於喜貪肆罪。

translations.literal: Sent out to inspect Xuanfu, he impeached the garrison eunuch Yu Xi for greedy and reckless crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to inspect Xuanfu, he impeached the garrison eunuch Yu Xi for greed and abuse of power.

sentences.zh: 為喜所訐，逮系詔獄，謫雲南河西典史。

translations.literal: Denounced by Xi, he was arrested and imprisoned in the imperial prison, then demoted to recorder of Hexi in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Denounced by Xi, he was seized and cast into the imperial prison, then demoted to recorder of Hexi in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，贈祭如張璞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shizong reign he was granted posthumous sacrificial honors like Zhang Pu.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Shizong reign he was granted posthumous sacrificial honors, as Zhang Pu had been.

sentences.zh: 毛思義，陽信人。

translations.literal: Mao Siyi was a native of Yangxin.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Siyi came from Yangxin.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the fifteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifteenth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 官永平知府。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Yongping.

sentences.zh: 正德十三年駕幸昌平，民間婦女驚避。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhengde, when the imperial carriage visited Changping, women among the people fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Zhengde, when the imperial carriage visited Changping, common women fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 思義下令言：「大喪未舉，車駕必不遠出。

translations.literal: Siyi issued an order saying: "The great mourning has not yet been completed; the imperial carriage will surely not travel far.
translations.idiomatic: Siyi issued an order declaring: "The great mourning has not yet been completed; the imperial carriage will not travel far.

sentences.zh: 非有文書，妄稱駕至擾民者，治以法。」

translations.literal: Without written orders, whoever falsely claims the carriage has arrived and harasses the people shall be punished by law."
translations.idiomatic: Without official writ, anyone who falsely claims the emperor is coming and harasses the people will be punished by law."

sentences.zh: 鎮守中官郭原與思義有隙，以聞。

translations.literal: The garrison eunuch Guo Yuan, who bore a grudge against Siyi, reported this.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison eunuch Guo Yuan, who bore a grudge against Siyi, reported the order to the throne.

sentences.zh: 立逮下詔獄，系半歲，謫雲南安寧知州。

translations.literal: He was immediately arrested and imprisoned in the imperial prison for half a year, then demoted to prefect of Anning in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately seized and thrown into the imperial prison for half a year, then demoted to prefect of Anning in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，累遷副都御史、應天巡撫。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign he rose in succession to Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing reign he rose to Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 胡文璧，耒陽人。

translations.literal: Hu Wenbi was a native of Leiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Wenbi came from Leiyang.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twelfth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twelfth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 正德初，由戶部郎中改御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde he was transferred from director in the Ministry of Revenue to censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhengde reign he was transferred from director in the Ministry of Revenue to censor.

sentences.zh: 出知鳳陽，遷天津副使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Fengyang, then promoted to vice commissioner of Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Fengyang, then promoted to vice commissioner of Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 中官張忠督直沽皇莊，縱群小牟利，文璧捕治之。

translations.literal: The eunuch Zhang Zhong supervised the imperial estate at Zhigu and let his followers profit; Wenbi arrested and punished them.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Zhang Zhong oversaw the imperial estate at Zhigu and let his followers extort profit; Wenbi arrested and punished them.

sentences.zh: 為所構，械系詔獄，謫延安府照磨。

translations.literal: Framed by Zhong, he was shackled and imprisoned in the imperial prison, then demoted to proofreader of Yan'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Framed by Zhong, he was shackled and cast into the imperial prison, then demoted to proofreader of Yan'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，累官四川按察使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing he rose in succession to surveillance commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jiajing reign he rose to surveillance commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 王相，光山人。

translations.literal: Wang Xiang was a native of Guangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang came from Guangshan.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the third year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 官御史。

translations.literal: He served as censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as censor.

sentences.zh: 十二年巡按山東。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was sent to inspect Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was sent to inspect Shandong.

sentences.zh: 鎮守中官黎鑒假進貢苛斂，相檄郡縣毋輒行。

translations.literal: The garrison eunuch Li Jian used tribute missions as a pretext for harsh levies; Xiang ordered the prefectures and counties not to comply at will.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison eunuch Li Jian used tribute missions as a pretext for harsh levies; Xiang ordered the prefectures and counties not to obey.

sentences.zh: 鑒怒，誣奏於朝。

translations.literal: Jian grew angry and lodged a false accusation at court.
translations.idiomatic: Jian flew into a rage and lodged a false accusation at court.

sentences.zh: 逮系詔獄，謫高郵判官。

translations.literal: Xiang was arrested and imprisoned in the imperial prison, then demoted to assistant magistrate of Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was seized and cast into the imperial prison, then demoted to assistant magistrate of Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jiajing reign he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 董相，嵩縣人。

translations.literal: Dong Xiang was a native of Song County.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xiang came from Song County.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the sixth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixth year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 官御史，巡視居庸諸關。

translations.literal: He served as censor and inspected the passes at Juyong and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: He served as censor with charge over the passes at Juyong and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 江彬遣小校米英執人於平谷，恃勢橫甚。

translations.literal: Jiang Bin sent a junior officer, Mi Ying, to seize people at Pinggu; relying on his power he was extremely overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Bin sent a junior officer, Mi Ying, to seize people at Pinggu, swaggering with impunity.

sentences.zh: 相收而仗之，將以聞。

translations.literal: Xiang arrested him and had him beaten with the staff, intending to report the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang arrested him, had him beaten with the staff, and prepared to report the matter.

sentences.zh: 彬遽譖於帝，械系詔獄，謫判徐州。

translations.literal: Bin quickly slandered him to the emperor; Xiang was shackled and imprisoned in the imperial prison, then demoted to assistant magistrate of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bin quickly denounced him to the emperor; Xiang was shackled and thrown into the imperial prison, then demoted to assistant magistrate of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，召復故官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing he was recalled to his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jiajing reign he was recalled to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 終山東副使。

translations.literal: He ended as vice commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as vice commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 劉士元，彭縣人。

translations.literal: Liu Shiyuan was a native of Peng County.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shiyuan came from Peng County.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the sixth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixth year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 官御史，巡按畿輔。

translations.literal: He served as censor and was sent to inspect the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: He served as censor with charge to inspect the capital region.

sentences.zh: 十三年，帝獵古北口，將招朵顏衛花當、把兒孫等燕勞。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the emperor hunted at Gubeikou and planned to summon Huadang and Ba'ersun of the Doyan Guard and others to a feast of reward and consolation.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the emperor hunted at Gubeikou and planned to summon Huadang, Ba'ersun, and others of the Doyan Guard to a feast of reward and consolation.

sentences.zh: 士元陳四不可。

translations.literal: Shiyuan set forth four reasons why this should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyuan argued that this should not be done on four grounds.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝幸河西務，指揮黃勛假供奉擾民，士元按之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor visited Hexiwu, the commander Huang Xun used the pretext of imperial service to harass the people; Shiyuan investigated him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor visited Hexiwu, the commander Huang Xun used the pretext of imperial service to harass the people, and Shiyuan investigated him.

sentences.zh: 勛懼，逃赴行在，因嬖幸譖於帝，云：士元聞駕至，令民間盡嫁其女，藏匿婦人。

translations.literal: Xun was afraid and fled to the imperial encampment; through a favored minion he slandered Shiyuan to the emperor, saying that upon hearing the imperial procession was coming, Shiyuan had ordered the people to marry off their daughters at once and conceal their women.
translations.idiomatic: Xun fled in fear to the imperial encampment and, through a favored minion, slandered Shiyuan to the emperor, claiming that upon hearing the imperial procession was approaching, Shiyuan had ordered the people to marry off their daughters at once and hide their women.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命裸縛面訊之。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry and ordered him stripped naked, bound, and interrogated face to face.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and ordered him stripped naked, bound, and interrogated in person.

sentences.zh: 野次無杖，取生柳幹痛笞之四十，幾死，囚檻車馳入京。

translations.literal: In the open field there were no beating staffs, so fresh willow branches were taken and he was flogged forty times with painful force; he nearly died, was imprisoned in a caged cart, and hurried to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the open field there were no beating staffs, so fresh willow branches were taken and he was flogged forty times until he nearly died; he was then locked in a caged cart and rushed to the capital.

sentences.zh: 並執知縣曹俊等十余人，同系詔獄。

translations.literal: The magistrate Cao Jun and more than ten others were also seized and imprisoned together in the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate Cao Jun and more than ten others were seized as well and imprisoned together in the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 都御史王璟及科道陳霑、牛天麟等交章論救，不報。

translations.literal: Chief Censor Wang Jing and the supervising secretaries Chen Zhan, Niu Tianlin, and others submitted successive memorials pleading for him; there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Censor Wang Jing and the supervising secretaries Chen Zhan, Niu Tianlin, and others submitted memorial after memorial pleading for him—but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 謫麟山驛丞。

translations.literal: He was demoted to assistant postmaster of Linshan.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to assistant postmaster of Linshan.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，復故官，出為湖州知府，遷湖廣副使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, he was restored to his former rank, sent out as prefect of Huzhou, and promoted to vice commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, Shiyuan was restored to his former rank, sent out as prefect of Huzhou, and promoted to vice commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 修荒政，積粟百萬余石。

translations.literal: He carried out famine relief measures and accumulated more than a million shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He carried out famine relief and stockpiled more than a million shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 事聞，被旌勞。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was commended and rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, he was commended and rewarded.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年，屢遷右副都御史，巡撫貴州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jiajing he was promoted in succession to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Jiajing he rose to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 居三年罷。

translations.literal: After three years in office he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 範輅，字以載，桂陽人。

translations.literal: Fan Lu, styled Yizai, was a native of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Lu, styled Yizai, came from Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the sixth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixth year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 授行人，除南京御史。

translations.literal: Appointed courier, then made censor at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed courier, then made censor at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 武宗久無子，輅偕同官請擇宗室賢者育宮中，以宋仁宗為法，不報。

translations.literal: The Wuzong Emperor long had no son; Lu together with colleagues in his office asked that a worthy member of the imperial clan be selected to be reared in the palace, taking Emperor Renzong of Song as the model; there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuzong Emperor long had no son; Lu and his colleagues asked that a worthy member of the imperial clan be selected and reared in the palace, taking Emperor Renzong of Song as the model—but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 先後劾中官黎安、劉瑯及衛官簡文、王忠罪。

translations.literal: In succession he impeached the eunuchs Li An and Liu Lang, and the guard officers Jian Wen and Wang Zhong, for their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In succession he impeached the eunuchs Li An and Liu Lang and the guard officers Jian Wen and Wang Zhong for their crimes.

sentences.zh: 又論馬姬有娠，不當入宮。

translations.literal: He also argued that Lady Ma, being pregnant, ought not enter the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Lady Ma, being with child, ought not enter the palace.

sentences.zh: 語皆切直。

translations.literal: His words were all sharp and forthright.
translations.idiomatic: In every case his words were sharp and forthright.

sentences.zh: 尋命清軍江西。

translations.literal: Before long he was ordered to inspect military households in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was ordered to inspect military households in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠令諸司以朝服見。

translations.literal: Prince Ning Chenhao ordered the various offices to receive visitors in court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ning Chenhao ordered the various offices to receive audiences in full court dress.

sentences.zh: 輅不可。

translations.literal: Lu refused.
translations.idiomatic: Lu refused.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「高帝定制，王府屬僚稱官。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The founding emperor established the system by which the retainers of princely establishments were addressed as officials.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The founding emperor established the system by which the retainers of princely establishments were addressed as officials.

sentences.zh: 後乃稱臣，其余文武及京官出使者皆稱官。

translations.literal: Later they came to be called subjects; the rest of civil and military officers, and capital officials sent out on missions, were all addressed as officials.
translations.idiomatic: Later they came to be called subjects; all other civil and military officers, and capital officials sent out on missions, were addressed as officials.

sentences.zh: 朝使相見以便服。

translations.literal: Envoys from court met one another in ordinary dress.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from court met one another in ordinary dress.

sentences.zh: 今天下王府儀註，制未畫一。

translations.literal: Today the ceremonial regulations of princely establishments throughout the realm are not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Today the ceremonial regulations of princely establishments throughout the realm are not uniform.

sentences.zh: 臣以為尊無二上，凡不稱臣者，皆不宜具朝服，以嚴大防。」

translations.literal: I hold that there is no second sovereign to be honored; all who are not called subjects ought not wear full court dress, so as to maintain a strict barrier."
translations.idiomatic: I hold that there is no second sovereign to be honored; all who are not called subjects ought not wear full court dress, so as to maintain a strict barrier."

sentences.zh: 章下禮官議。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the ritual officials for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was sent down to the ritual officials for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 宸濠馳疏爭之，廷議請如輅言。

translations.literal: Chenhao sent an urgent memorial arguing the point; court deliberation requested compliance with Lu's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao sent an urgent memorial contesting the point, but court deliberation recommended adopting Lu's proposal.

sentences.zh: 宸濠伶人秦榮僭侈，輅劾治之。

translations.literal: Chenhao's actor Qin Rong was presumptuous and extravagant; Lu impeached and punished him.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao's actor Qin Rong was presumptuous and extravagant; Lu impeached him and had him punished.

sentences.zh: 又劾鎮守太監畢真貪虐十五事，疏留不下。

translations.literal: He also impeached the garrison eunuch Bi Zhen on fifteen counts of greed and cruelty; the memorial was detained and not forwarded.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached the garrison eunuch Bi Zhen on fifteen counts of greed and cruelty, but the memorial was detained and never forwarded.

sentences.zh: 真乃摭他事誣之，遂逮下詔獄。

translations.literal: Zhen then gathered other matters to frame him falsely, and Lu was arrested and cast into the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen then gathered other matters to frame him falsely, and Lu was arrested and thrown into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 值帝巡幸，淹系經年。

translations.literal: At a time when the emperor was on tour, he remained imprisoned for more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was on tour, he remained imprisoned for more than a year.

sentences.zh: 至十四年四月始謫龍州宣撫司經歷。

translations.literal: Only in the fourth month of the fourteenth year was he demoted to administrator of Longzhou Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the fourth month of the fourteenth year was he demoted to administrator of the Longzhou Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 未幾，宸濠及真謀逆誅，御史謝源、伍希儒等交章薦輅。

translations.literal: Before long Chenhao and Zhen were executed for plotting rebellion; Censors Xie Yuan, Wu Xiru, and others submitted successive memorials recommending Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chenhao and Zhen were executed for plotting rebellion; Censors Xie Yuan, Wu Xiru, and others submitted memorial after memorial recommending Lu.

sentences.zh: 未及召，世宗立，復故官。

translations.literal: Before he could be summoned, Emperor Shizong ascended the throne and Lu was restored to his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could be summoned, Emperor Shizong ascended the throne and Lu was restored to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 遷福建僉事，轉江西副使，致仕歸。

translations.literal: He was promoted to commissioner of Fujian, transferred to vice commissioner of Jiangxi, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commissioner of Fujian, transferred to vice commissioner of Jiangxi, and retired.

sentences.zh: 又用胡世寧薦，起密雲兵備副使。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Hu Shining he was recalled to serve as vice commissioner for military preparedness at Miyun.
translations.idiomatic: On Hu Shining's recommendation he was recalled to serve as vice commissioner for military preparedness at Miyun.

sentences.zh: 討礦賊有功，歷江西、福建左、右布政使。

translations.literal: He had merit in suppressing mining bandits and rose in succession to Left and Right Provincial Administrators of Jiangxi and Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He had merit in suppressing mining bandits and rose in succession to Left and Right Provincial Administrator of Jiangxi and Fujian.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 張欽，字敬之，順天通州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Qin, styled Jingzhi, was a native of Tongzhou in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qin, styled Jingzhi, came from Tongzhou in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the sixth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixth year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 由行人授御史，巡視居庸諸關。

translations.literal: From courier he was appointed censor with charge to inspect the passes at Juyong and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: From courier he was appointed censor with charge over the passes at Juyong and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 十二年七月，帝聽江彬言，將出關幸宣府。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twelfth year the emperor, heeding Jiang Bin's words, planned to leave the pass and visit Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twelfth year the emperor, heeding Jiang Bin, planned to leave the pass and visit Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 欽上疏諫曰：「臣聞明主不惡切直之言以納忠，烈士不憚死亡之誅以極諫。

translations.literal: Qin submitted a remonstrance, saying: "I have heard that a wise ruler does not despise blunt, forthright words when accepting loyal counsel, and that a man of fierce loyalty does not fear the death penalty that follows extreme remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Qin submitted a remonstrance, saying: "I have heard that a wise ruler does not despise blunt, forthright words when accepting loyal counsel, and that a man of fierce loyalty does not fear the death penalty that follows extreme remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 比者，人言紛紛，謂車駕欲度居庸，遠遊邊塞。

translations.literal: Recently rumor has swirled that the imperial carriage intends to cross Juyong and travel far into the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: Recently rumor has swirled that the imperial carriage intends to cross Juyong and travel far into the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 臣度陛下非漫遊，蓋欲親征北寇也。

translations.literal: I judge that Your Majesty does not aim at idle wandering, but likely intends a personal campaign against the northern raiders.
translations.idiomatic: I judge that Your Majesty does not aim at idle wandering, but likely intends a personal campaign against the northern raiders.

sentences.zh: 不知北寇猖獗，但可遣將徂征，豈宜親勞萬乘？

translations.literal: Do you not know that the northern raiders are rampant? Generals may be dispatched to lead the expedition—how can the Son of Heaven himself be troubled?
translations.idiomatic: Do you not know that the northern raiders are rampant? Generals may be dispatched to lead the expedition—how can the Son of Heaven himself be troubled?

sentences.zh: 英宗不聽大臣言，六師遠駕，遂成己巳之變。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong did not heed his ministers; the six armies rode far afield, and so arose the disaster of the Jisi year.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong did not heed his ministers; the six armies rode far afield, and so arose the disaster of the Jisi year.

sentences.zh: 且匹夫猶不自輕，陛下奈何以宗廟社稷之身蹈不測之險。

translations.literal: Even a common man does not lightly risk himself—how can Your Majesty, bearer of the ancestral temples and altars of state, tread into immeasurable peril?
translations.idiomatic: Even a common man does not lightly risk himself—how can Your Majesty, bearer of the ancestral temples and altars of state, tread into immeasurable peril?

sentences.zh: 今內無親王監國，又無太子臨朝。

translations.literal: Within there is no imperial prince to supervise the realm, and no crown prince to preside over court.
translations.idiomatic: Within there is no imperial prince to supervise the realm, and no crown prince to preside over court.

sentences.zh: 外之甘肅有土番之患，江右有皞賊之擾，淮南有漕運之艱，巴蜀有采辦之困；

translations.literal: Abroad: Gansu suffers from Turfan troubles; the right bank of the Yangzi has Hao bandit disturbances; the Huai region faces hardships in grain transport; Bashu is afflicted by procurement burdens;
translations.idiomatic: Abroad: Gansu suffers from Turfan troubles; Jiangyou is disturbed by Hao bandits; the Huai region faces hardships in grain transport; Bashu is afflicted by procurement burdens;

sentences.zh: 京畿諸郡夏麥少收，秋潦為沴。

translations.literal: The capital districts have had a poor summer wheat harvest and autumn flooding has brought disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The capital districts have had a poor summer wheat harvest, and autumn flooding has brought disaster.

sentences.zh: 而陛下不虞禍變，欲縱轡長驅，觀兵絕塞，臣竊危已。」

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty does not guard against calamity and change, but wishes to loosen the reins and ride far to display arms beyond the frontier passes—I, your servant, am deeply alarmed."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty does not guard against calamity and change, but wishes to loosen the reins and ride far to display arms beyond the frontier passes—I, your servant, am deeply alarmed."

sentences.zh: 已，聞朝臣切諫皆不納，復疏言：「臣愚以為乘輿不可出者有三：人心搖動，供億浩繁，一也；

translations.literal: Thereafter, learning that the earnest remonstrance of court ministers had all gone unheeded, he submitted another memorial: "In my foolish view there are three reasons the imperial carriage must not leave: public hearts are unsettled and provisioning is vast and costly—the first;
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, learning that the earnest remonstrance of court ministers had all gone unheeded, he submitted another memorial: "In my foolish view there are three reasons the imperial carriage must not leave: public hearts are unsettled and provisioning is vast and costly—the first;

sentences.zh: 遠涉險阻，兩宮懸念，二也；

translations.literal: crossing distant perilous routes while the two palaces are left in anxious suspense—the second;
translations.idiomatic: crossing distant perilous routes while the two palaces are left in anxious suspense—the second;

sentences.zh: 北寇方張，難與之角，三也。

translations.literal: the northern raiders are swelling in strength and are hard to contend with—the third.
translations.idiomatic: the northern raiders are swelling in strength and are hard to contend with—the third.

sentences.zh: 臣職居言路，奉詔巡關，分當效死，不敢愛身以負陛下。」

translations.literal: My duty lies on the remonstrance track; by imperial order I inspect the passes, and in duty bound I should give my life—I dare not spare my person and fail Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: My duty lies on the remonstrance track; by imperial order I inspect the passes, and in duty bound I should give my life—I dare not spare my person and fail Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 疏入，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted; there was no reply.

sentences.zh: 八月朔，帝微行至昌平，傳報出關甚急。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eighth month the emperor went in disguise to Changping; urgent reports said he would leave the pass at once.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eighth month the emperor went in disguise to Changping; urgent reports said he would leave the pass at once.

sentences.zh: 欽命指揮孫璽閉關，納門鑰藏之。

translations.literal: Qin ordered the commander Sun Xi to shut the pass, take in the gate keys, and hide them.
translations.idiomatic: Qin ordered the commander Sun Xi to shut the pass, take in the gate keys, and hide them.

sentences.zh: 分守中官劉嵩欲詣昌平朝謁，欽止之曰：「車駕將出關，是我與君今日死生之會也。

translations.literal: The eunuch Liu Song, stationed to share defense, wished to go to Changping for an audience; Qin stopped him, saying: "The imperial carriage is about to leave the pass—today is the day when you and I meet life or death.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Liu Song, stationed to share defense, wished to go to Changping for an audience; Qin stopped him, saying: "The imperial carriage is about to leave the pass—today is the day when you and I meet life or death.

sentences.zh: 關不開，車駕不得出，違天子命，當死。

translations.literal: If the pass is not opened the imperial carriage cannot leave—we would defy the Son of Heaven's command and must die.
translations.idiomatic: If the pass is not opened the imperial carriage cannot leave—we would defy the Son of Heaven's command and must die.

sentences.zh: 關開，車駕得出，天下事不可知。

translations.literal: If the pass is opened and the imperial carriage can leave, affairs under Heaven become unknowable.
translations.idiomatic: If the pass is opened and the imperial carriage can leave, affairs under Heaven become unknowable.

sentences.zh: 萬一有如『土木』，我與君亦死。

translations.literal: Should anything like 'Tumu' occur, you and I die as well.
translations.idiomatic: Should anything like 'Tumu' occur, you and I die as well.

sentences.zh: 寧坐不開關死，死且不朽。」

translations.literal: Better to die for keeping the pass closed—death and yet imperishable fame."
translations.idiomatic: Better to die for keeping the pass closed—death and yet imperishable fame."

sentences.zh: 頃之，帝召璽。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor summoned Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor summoned Xi.

sentences.zh: 璽曰：「御史在，臣不敢擅離。」

translations.literal: Xi said: "The censor is here; your servant dares not leave without permission."
translations.idiomatic: Xi said: "The censor is here; your servant dares not leave without permission."

sentences.zh: 乃更召嵩。

translations.literal: The emperor then summoned Song instead.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then summoned Song instead.

sentences.zh: 嵩謂欽曰：「吾主上家奴也，敢不赴。」

translations.literal: Song said to Qin: "I am the household slave of our lord—how dare I not go."
translations.idiomatic: Song said to Qin: "I am the household slave of our lord—how dare I not go."

sentences.zh: 欽因負敕印手劍坐關門下曰：「敢言開關者，斬。」

translations.literal: Qin then shouldered the imperial rescript seal and hand sword and sat beneath the gate, saying: "Whoever speaks of opening the pass—beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: Qin then shouldered the imperial rescript seal and hand sword and sat beneath the gate, saying: "Whoever speaks of opening the pass—beheaded."

sentences.zh: 夜草疏曰：「臣聞天子將有親征之事，必先期下詔廷臣集議。

translations.literal: At night he drafted a memorial: "I have heard that when the Son of Heaven is to undertake a personal campaign, he must first fix a date, issue an edict, and convene court ministers for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: At night he drafted a memorial: "I have heard that when the Son of Heaven is to undertake a personal campaign, he must first fix a date, issue an edict, and convene court ministers for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 其行也，六軍翼衛，百官扈從，而後有車馬之音，羽旄之美。

translations.literal: When he departs, the six armies flank and guard him and officials attend in escort—only then come the sound of chariots and horses and the glory of banners and feathered standards.
translations.idiomatic: When he departs, the six armies flank and guard him and officials attend in escort—only then come the sound of chariots and horses and the glory of banners and feathered standards.

sentences.zh: 今寂然一不聞，輒雲『車駕即日過關』，此必有假陛下名出邊勾賊者。

translations.literal: Now all is silent and nothing is heard, yet it is suddenly said 'the imperial carriage will cross the pass this very day'—there must be someone using Your Majesty's name to leave the frontier and collude with bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Now all is silent and nothing is heard, yet it is suddenly said 'the imperial carriage will cross the pass this very day'—there must be someone using Your Majesty's name to leave the frontier and collude with bandits.

sentences.zh: 臣請捕其人，明正典刑。

translations.literal: I request that this person be seized and punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: I request that this person be seized and punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 若陛下果欲出關，必兩宮用寶，臣乃敢開。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly wishes to leave the pass, the seals of the two palaces must be affixed—only then dare I open it.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly wishes to leave the pass, the seals of the two palaces must be affixed—only then dare I open it.

sentences.zh: 不然萬死不奉詔。」

translations.literal: Otherwise I will defy the command unto ten thousand deaths."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I will defy the command unto ten thousand deaths."

sentences.zh: 奏未達，使者復來。

translations.literal: Before the memorial arrived, messengers came again.
translations.idiomatic: Before the memorial arrived, messengers came again.

sentences.zh: 欽拔劍叱之曰：「此詐也。」

translations.literal: Qin drew his sword and shouted at them: "This is fraud."
translations.idiomatic: Qin drew his sword and shouted at them: "This is fraud."

sentences.zh: 使者懼而返，為帝言「張御史幾殺臣」。

translations.literal: The messengers fled in fear and reported to the emperor, "Censor Zhang nearly killed us."
translations.idiomatic: The messengers fled in fear and reported to the emperor, "Censor Zhang nearly killed us."

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，顧朱寧：「為我趣捕殺御史。」

translations.literal: The emperor flew into a rage and turned to Zhu Ning: "Go seize and kill the censor for me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and turned to Zhu Ning: "Go seize and kill the censor for me."

sentences.zh: 會梁儲、蔣冕等追至沙河，請帝歸京師。

translations.literal: Just then Liang Chu, Jiang Mian, and others caught up at Shahe and asked the emperor to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Liang Chu, Jiang Mian, and others caught up at Shahe and asked the emperor to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝徘徊未決，而欽疏亦至，廷臣又多諫者，帝不得已乃自昌平還，意怏怏未已。

translations.literal: The emperor hesitated undecided; Qin's memorial also arrived, and many in court remonstrated as well—the emperor had no choice but to return from Changping, though resentment lingered.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated undecided; Qin's memorial also arrived, and many in court remonstrated as well—the emperor had no choice but to return from Changping, though resentment lingered.

sentences.zh: 又二十余日，欽巡白羊口。

translations.literal: After more than twenty days Qin was inspecting Baiyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: After more than twenty days Qin was inspecting Baiyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 帝微服自德勝門出，夜宿羊房民舍，遂疾馳出關，數問「御史安在」？

translations.literal: The emperor, in plain dress, left through Desheng Gate, lodged overnight in a commoner's house at Yangfang, then raced through the pass, repeatedly asking "Where is the censor?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, in plain dress, left through Desheng Gate, lodged overnight in a commoner's house at Yangfang, then raced through the pass, repeatedly asking, "Where is the censor?"

sentences.zh: 欽聞，追之，已不及。

translations.literal: Qin heard of it and pursued him, but could not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: Qin heard of it and pursued him, but could not overtake him.

sentences.zh: 欲再疏諫，而帝使中官谷大用守關，禁毋得出一人。

translations.literal: He wished to remonstrate again, but the emperor had the eunuch Gu Dayong guard the pass and forbid anyone from leaving.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to remonstrate again, but the emperor had the eunuch Gu Dayong guard the pass and forbid anyone from leaving.

sentences.zh: 欽感憤，西望痛哭。

translations.literal: Qin, moved to anguish, wept facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Qin, moved to anguish, wept facing west.

sentences.zh: 於是京師盛傳「張御史閉關三疏」雲。

translations.literal: Thereupon the capital widely repeated the saying "Censor Zhang shut the pass with three memorials."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the capital widely repeated the saying "Censor Zhang shut the pass with three memorials."

sentences.zh: 明年，帝從宣府還。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor returned from Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor returned from Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 至關，笑曰：「前御史阻我，我今已歸矣」，然亦不之罪也。

translations.literal: When he reached the pass he smiled and said, "The former censor blocked me—I have returned now," yet he did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the pass he smiled and said, "The former censor blocked me—I have returned now," yet he did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，出為漢中知府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong succeeded to the throne, Qin was sent out as prefect of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong succeeded to the throne, Qin was sent out as prefect of Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 累官太仆卿。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十七年以右副都御史巡撫四川。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Jiajing he served as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Jiajing he served as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 召為工部左侍郎，被論罷。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Left Vice Minister of Works, then dismissed after impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Left Vice Minister of Works, then dismissed after impeachment.

sentences.zh: 欽初姓李。

translations.literal: Qin originally bore the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: Qin originally bore the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 既通顯，始復其姓。

translations.literal: Once he had risen to prominence, he at last restored his original surname.
translations.idiomatic: Only after he had risen to prominence did he at last restore his original surname.

sentences.zh: 事父母孝。

translations.literal: He served his parents with filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: He was filial toward his parents.

sentences.zh: 有不悅，長跪請，至解乃已。

translations.literal: When they were displeased, he would kneel for a long time and plead until their anger was dispelled.
translations.idiomatic: When they were displeased, he would kneel and plead at length until their anger had passed.

sentences.zh: 周廣，字克之，昆山人。

translations.literal: Zhou Guang, styled Kezhi, was a native of Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Guang, styled Kezhi, came from Kunshan.

sentences.zh: 弘治十八年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the eighteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the eighteenth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 歷知莆田、吉水二縣。

translations.literal: He served in succession as magistrate of Putian and Jishui counties.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as magistrate of Putian and Jishui counties.

sentences.zh: 正德中，以治最征授御史，疏陳四事，略言：

translations.literal: During the Zhengde reign, summoned for outstanding governance and appointed censor, he submitted a memorial setting forth four matters, saying in summary:
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign he was summoned for outstanding governance and appointed censor; in a memorial setting forth four matters he wrote, in summary:

sentences.zh: 三代以前，未有佛法。

translations.literal: Before the Three Dynasties there was no Buddhist teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Three Dynasties there was no Buddhist teaching.

sentences.zh: 況剌麻尤釋教所不齒。

translations.literal: Moreover, lamas are especially despised even within Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: Lamas, moreover, are held in contempt even within Buddhism itself.

sentences.zh: 耳貫銅環，身衣赭服，殘破禮法，肆為淫邪。

translations.literal: They wear copper rings through their ears and ochre robes on their bodies, mutilating ritual and law and indulging in lewd wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: With copper rings in their ears and ochre robes on their bodies, they trample ritual and law and indulge in lewd wickedness.

sentences.zh: 宜投四裔，以禦魑魅。

translations.literal: They ought to be cast out to the four borderlands to ward off demons.
translations.idiomatic: They ought to be cast out to the four borderlands to keep demons at bay.

sentences.zh: 奈何令近君側，為群盜興兵口實哉！

translations.literal: How can they be allowed near the ruler's side and furnish rebels with a pretext for raising arms!
translations.idiomatic: How can they be allowed near the ruler's side and furnish rebels with a pretext for taking up arms!

sentences.zh: 昔禹戒舜曰：「毋若丹朱傲，惟慢遊是好。」

translations.literal: In antiquity Yu admonished Shun, saying: "Do not be like the arrogant Danzhu, who loved only idle wandering."
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Yu admonished Shun, saying: "Do not be like the arrogant Danzhu, who loved nothing but idle wandering."

sentences.zh: 周公戒成王曰：「毋若商王紂之迷亂，酗於酒德。」

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou admonished King Cheng, saying: "Do not be like King Zhou of Shang in his deluded disorder, drunken in the virtue of wine."
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou admonished King Cheng, saying: "Do not be like King Zhou of Shang in his deluded disorder, drunken in the virtue of wine."

sentences.zh: 今之伶人，助慢遊迷亂者也。

translations.literal: Today's actors are those who abet idle wandering and deluded disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Today's actors are precisely those who abet idle wandering and deluded disorder.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗與伶官戲狎，一夫夜呼，倉皇出走。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang frolicked intimately with actor-officials; one night a man cried out and he fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang frolicked intimately with actor-officials; one night a man cried out, and he fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜遣逐樂工，不得籍之禁內，乃所以放鄭聲也。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that musicians ought to be driven away and not registered within the forbidden precincts—this is how licentious music is banished.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that musicians ought to be driven away and not registered within the forbidden precincts—this is how licentious music is banished.

sentences.zh: 陛下承祖宗統緒，而群小獻媚熒惑，致三宮鎖怨，蘭殿無征。

translations.literal: Your Majesty inherits the imperial line of the ancestral house, yet petty men offer flattery and beguilement, so that the three palaces are locked in resentment and the orchid hall knows no auspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty inherits the imperial line of the ancestral house, yet petty men offer flattery and beguilement, so that the three palaces are locked in resentment and the orchid hall knows no auspicious sign.

sentences.zh: 雖陛下春秋鼎盛，獨不思萬世計乎？

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty is in the prime of life, will you alone give no thought to the plan of ten thousand generations?
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty is in the prime of life, will you give no thought to the plan of ten thousand generations?

sentences.zh: 中人稍有資產，猶畜妾媵以圖嗣續。

translations.literal: Even a man of moderate means, if he has some property, still keeps concubines to seek continuation of his line.
translations.idiomatic: Even a man of moderate means, if he has some property, still keeps concubines in hope of continuing his line.

sentences.zh: 未有專養螟蛉，不顧祖宗繼嗣者也。

translations.literal: There has never been one who devoted himself solely to rearing an adopted son and paid no heed to ancestral succession.
translations.idiomatic: There has never been one who devoted himself solely to rearing an adopted son and paid no heed to ancestral succession.

sentences.zh: 義子錢寧本宦豎蒼頭，濫寵已極，乃復攘兌攵貨賄，輕蔑王章。

translations.literal: The adopted son Qian Ning was originally a eunuch's menial servant; favor lavished on him has already reached its limit, yet he also seizes goods and accepts bribes and treats the royal statutes with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: The adopted son Qian Ning was originally a eunuch's menial servant; favor lavished on him has already reached its limit, yet he also seizes goods and accepts bribes and treats the royal statutes with contempt.

sentences.zh: 甚至投刺於人，自稱皇庶子。

translations.literal: He even handed out calling cards to others and styled himself an imperial bastard son.
translations.idiomatic: He even handed out calling cards to others and styled himself an imperial bastard son.

sentences.zh: 僭逾之罪所不忍言。

translations.literal: The crime of presumptuous overreach is more than one can bear to speak.
translations.idiomatic: The crime of presumptuous overreach is more than one can bear to speak.

sentences.zh: 陛下何不慎選宗室之賢者，置諸左右，以待皇嗣之生。

translations.literal: Why does Your Majesty not carefully select worthy members of the imperial clan, place them at hand, and wait for the birth of an imperial heir?
translations.idiomatic: Why does Your Majesty not carefully select worthy members of the imperial clan, place them at hand, and wait for the birth of an imperial heir?

sentences.zh: 諸義兒、養子俱奪其名爵，乃所以遠佞人也。

translations.literal: All adopted sons and foster sons should be stripped of their titles and ranks—this is how sycophants are kept at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: All adopted sons and foster sons should be stripped of their titles and ranks—this is how sycophants are kept at a distance.

sentences.zh: 近兩京言官論大臣禦寇不職者，陛下率優容，即武將失律亦赦不誅。

translations.literal: Lately, when censors of the two capitals criticized grand ministers for failing in their duty to repel invaders, Your Majesty has generally shown leniency; even when military commanders violated discipline, they were pardoned and not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, when censors of the two capitals criticized grand ministers for failing in their duty to repel invaders, Your Majesty has generally shown leniency; even when military commanders violated discipline, they were pardoned and not punished.

sentences.zh: 故兵氣不揚，功成無日，川原白骨，積如丘山。

translations.literal: Hence martial spirit does not rise, success is nowhere in sight, and white bones on field and plain pile up like hills.
translations.idiomatic: Hence martial spirit does not rise, victory seems nowhere in sight, and white bones on field and plain pile up like hills.

sentences.zh: 夫出師十萬，日費千金。

translations.literal: When an army of a hundred thousand is dispatched, a thousand in gold is spent each day.
translations.idiomatic: When an army of a hundred thousand is dispatched, a thousand in gold is spent each day.

sentences.zh: 今海內困憊已骨見而肉消矣，諸統兵大臣如陳金、陸完輩可任其優遊玩寇，不加切責哉！

translations.literal: Now the realm is exhausted to the bone and wasted to the flesh—can commanders-in-chief such as Chen Jin and Lu Wan be allowed to roam at ease and toy with the enemy without stern rebuke!
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is exhausted to the bone—can commanders-in-chief such as Chen Jin and Lu Wan be allowed to roam at ease and toy with the enemy without stern rebuke!

sentences.zh: 請定期責令成功，以贖前罪。

translations.literal: I request that a deadline be set and success demanded of them, so that they may atone for their former crimes.
translations.idiomatic: I request that a deadline be set and success demanded of them, so that they may atone for their former crimes.

sentences.zh: 寧見疏大怒，留之不下，傳旨謫廣東懷遠驛丞。

translations.literal: Ning, upon seeing the memorial, flew into a rage; it was detained and not forwarded, and an edict was issued demoting Guang to assistant postmaster of Huaiyuan in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Ning, upon seeing the memorial, flew into a rage; it was detained and not forwarded, and an edict was issued demoting Guang to assistant postmaster of Huaiyuan in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 主事曹琥救之，亦被謫。

translations.literal: The director Cao Hu pleaded for him and was also demoted.
translations.idiomatic: The director Cao Hu pleaded for him and was demoted as well.

sentences.zh: 寧怒不已，使人遮道刺廣。

translations.literal: Ning's anger did not cease, and he sent men to lie in wait along the road and assassinate Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Ning's anger did not cease, and he sent men to lie in wait along the road and assassinate Guang.

sentences.zh: 廣知之，易姓名，變服，潛行四百余裏乃免。

translations.literal: Guang learned of it, changed his name, altered his dress, and traveled secretly more than four hundred li before escaping harm.
translations.idiomatic: Guang learned of it, changed his name, altered his dress, and traveled secretly more than four hundred li before he was safe.

sentences.zh: 武定侯郭勛鎮廣東，承寧風旨以白金試廣，廣拒不受。

translations.literal: Marquis Wuding Guo Xun governed Guangdong; following Ning's intent he tested Guang with white silver, but Guang refused to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Wuding Guo Xun governed Guangdong; following Ning's intent he tested Guang with white silver, but Guang refused to accept it.

sentences.zh: 伺廣謁御史，攝致軍門，箠系幾死，御史救之始解。

translations.literal: Waiting until Guang came to pay his respects to the censor, he had him seized and brought to the military headquarters, beaten and bound until he nearly died; only when the censor rescued him was he released.
translations.idiomatic: Waiting until Guang came to pay his respects to the censor, he had him seized and brought to the military headquarters, beaten and bound until he nearly died; only when the censor rescued him was he released.

sentences.zh: 越二年，遷建昌知縣，有惠政。

translations.literal: After two years he was transferred to magistrate of Jianchang, where his benevolent governance won praise.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was transferred to magistrate of Jianchang, where his benevolent governance won praise.

sentences.zh: 寧矯旨再謫竹寨驛丞。

translations.literal: Ning forged an edict and had him demoted again to assistant postmaster of Zhuzhai.
translations.idiomatic: Ning forged an edict and had him demoted again to assistant postmaster of Zhuzhai.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，復故官，歷江西副使，提督學校。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, Guang was restored to his former rank, served as vice commissioner of Jiangxi, and supervised the schools.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, Guang was restored to his former rank, served as vice commissioner of Jiangxi, and supervised the schools.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年舉治行卓異，擢福建按察使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing he was cited for outstanding governance and promoted to surveillance commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiajing he was cited for outstanding governance and promoted to surveillance commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 鎮守中官以百金饋，廣貯之庫，將劾之。

translations.literal: The garrison eunuch presented him with a hundred in gold; Guang stored it in the treasury and prepared to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison eunuch presented him with a hundred in gold; Guang stored it in the treasury and prepared to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 中官懼，謝罪，自是不敢撓。

translations.literal: The eunuch was afraid and apologized; from then on he did not dare interfere.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch was afraid and apologized; from then on he did not dare interfere.

sentences.zh: 六年，以右僉都御史巡撫江西，墨吏望風去。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he served as Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Jiangxi; corrupt officials fled at the mere report of his coming.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he served as Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Jiangxi; corrupt officials fled at the mere report of his coming.

sentences.zh: 將限豪右田，不果。

translations.literal: He planned to limit the landholdings of powerful families, but the plan did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: He planned to limit the landholdings of powerful families, but the plan did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 明年拜南京刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Right Vice Minister of Justice at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was appointed Right Vice Minister of Justice at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 居二年，暴疾卒。

translations.literal: After two years in office he died suddenly of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After two years in office he died suddenly of illness.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖末，贈右都御史。

translations.literal: At the end of Jiajing he was posthumously made Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jiajing reign he was posthumously made Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 廣初以鄉舉入太學，師章懋。

translations.literal: Guang first entered the Imperial Academy through the provincial examination and studied under Zhang Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Guang first entered the Imperial Academy through the provincial examination and studied under Zhang Mao.

sentences.zh: 在裏闬，與魏校友善。

translations.literal: In his home district he was on friendly terms with Wei Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: In his home district he was on friendly terms with Wei Xiao.

sentences.zh: 平生嚴冷無笑容。

translations.literal: All his life he was stern and cold and never smiled.
translations.idiomatic: All his life he was stern and cold and never smiled.

sentences.zh: 居官公強，弗受請托，士類莫不憚之。

translations.literal: In office he was upright and firm, accepted no private requests, and men of learning all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was upright and firm, accepted no private requests, and men of learning all feared him.

sentences.zh: 曹琥，字瑞卿，巢人。

translations.literal: Cao Hu, styled Ruiqing, was a native of Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hu, styled Ruiqing, came from Chao.

sentences.zh: 弘治十八年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the eighteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the eighteenth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 授南京工部主事，改戶部。

translations.literal: Appointed director in the Nanjing Ministry of Works, then transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director in the Nanjing Ministry of Works, then transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 既抗疏救廣，吏部擬調河南通判。

translations.literal: After he submitted a bold memorial pleading for Guang, the Ministry of Personnel proposed transferring him to vice prefect of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: After he submitted a bold memorial pleading for Guang, the Ministry of Personnel proposed transferring him to vice prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 寧欲遠竄，乃改尋甸，再遷廣信同知。

translations.literal: Ning wished to banish him far away, so the appointment was changed to Xundian, and he was later transferred to vice prefect of Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: Ning wished to banish him far away, so the appointment was changed to Xundian, and he was later transferred to vice prefect of Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 寧王暨鎮守中貴托貢獻，頻有征斂。

translations.literal: Prince Ning and the garrison eunuchs used tribute missions as a pretext and repeatedly imposed levies.
